This method may require more manual configuration and maintenance compared to using the built-in approvals feature.

explanation: Why reinvent the wheel? SharePoint's built-in Approvals flows are great, and using the information in this module you can set them up quickly and easily.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company rolling out Power Platform wants to make sure access to apps, data, and environments stays secure. Which of these components are actually used to manage security and control access in Power Platform?

options.explanation: Security Roles in Dataverse are used to manage access to data within the Power Platform. By assigning specific security roles to users, administrators can control who can view, edit, or delete data in Dataverse tables, ensuring secure access to apps and data.

Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Policies are essential for managing and controlling the flow of sensitive data within the Power Platform. These policies help prevent data leakage by monitoring and restricting the sharing of sensitive information across apps, ensuring secure access to environments.

Power BI Dashboards are primarily used for data visualization and reporting within the Power Platform. While they provide valuable insights, they are not directly related to managing security and controlling access to apps, data, and environments.

Environment Roles, such as Admin, Maker, and User, play a crucial role in managing security and controlling access within the Power Platform. These roles define the level of access and permissions users have within specific environments, ensuring secure access to apps and data.

Solution Checker is a tool within the Power Platform that helps identify potential issues and best practices in solutions. While it can assist in ensuring the quality of solutions, it is not directly related to managing security and controlling access in the Power Platform.

Connectors in the Power Platform are used to establish connections to external data sources and services. While they are essential for integrating data and services, they are not specifically used to manage security and control access within the Power Platform.

explanation: A. Security Roles in DataverseMicrosoft Dataverse security roles control what users can do with data, including permissions to read, create, update, or delete records. They manage table-level and record-level access within the environment. B. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) PoliciesDLP policies control how connectors can be used together and help prevent sensitive data from being shared improperly across business and non-business services. D. Environment RolesEnvironment roles define user permissions at the environment level, such as who can be an admin, maker, or standard user, and what actions they can perform in that environment.

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: Your team deals with repetitive, error-prone data entry every time a project kicks off, hurting both efficiency and accuracy. Which Power Platform tool would streamline this and cut down on errors?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Power Apps is a platform that allows users to create custom business applications without the need for extensive coding knowledge. While it can be used to streamline data entry processes, Power Automate is more suitable for automating repetitive tasks and workflows, making it the better choice for addressing the challenges related to basic data entry in this scenario.

Power Automate, formerly known as Microsoft Flow, is a platform that enables users to automate workflows and tasks across various applications and services. In the context of the given scenario, Power Automate can be utilized to automate the data entry process, reducing errors and enhancing efficiency by eliminating the need for manual input across different divisions.

This option is incorrect. Power Pages is a low-code platform that enables users to create secure, data-driven websites with minimal technical expertise. It is ideal for businesses and organizations looking to build customer portals, employee dashboards, or public-facing web apps integrated with Microsoft Dataverse. With customizable templates and responsive design, Power Pages streamlines web development while maintaining security and scalability

explanation: The correct answer is Power Automate. If you understand the applications of various applications, you will be able to answer the question. Power Apps: Expense Reporting App: Create a mobile app where employees can easily enter and submit their expenses, including receipts and details, streamlining the expense reporting process. Customer Feedback Form: Build a form-based app for collecting customer feedback, which can be accessed by support teams to improve services and products. Inventory Management: Develop an app to track inventory levels, automate reorder notifications, and manage stock across different locations efficiently. Power Automate: Email Notification Workflow: Set up a workflow that sends automatic email notifications to team members when a new task is assigned or when specific conditions are met. Approval Process Automation: Design an automated approval workflow for purchase requests, where managers can review and approve requests with a single click. Data Integration: Create a workflow that extracts data from one application (e.g., SharePoint) and updates it in another (e.g., CRM), ensuring data consistency. Power Copilot Studio: Customer Support Chatbot: Build a virtual agent to assist customers with common inquiries, such as tracking orders, troubleshooting issues, and accessing FAQs. HR Assistant: Create a virtual agent for employees to ask HR-related questions, such as vacation requests, benefits information, or onboarding procedures. Appointment Scheduling Bot: Develop a bot that helps users book appointments, whether for medical consultations, service appointments, or meetings with sales representatives. Power Pages: Customer Self-Service Portal: Develop a page where customers can log in, access their account information, view invoices, and submit support tickets without needing assistance. Employee Training Portal: Create a  page for employees to enrol in training courses, track their progress, and access learning resources. Community Forum: Build a community pages for users to engage in discussions, share knowledge, and collaborate on topics related to your products or services. These use cases demonstrate how each component of the Power Platform can be applied to various business scenarios, improving efficiency, automation, data analysis, and customer engagement.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Adding an item in SharePoint causes a Power Automate workflow to kick off. What type of operation is being used to start that workflow?

options.explanation: The correct choice is "Trigger" because in Power Automate, a trigger is an event that starts a workflow. In this scenario, the item added in SharePoint acts as a trigger that initiates the workflow in Power Automate. Example of a SharePoint Trigger in Power Automate: Trigger: When an item is created in SharePoint. Action: Send an approval request to a manager. Result: Once a new item is added, the workflow automatically initiates the approval process.

The choice "Action" is incorrect because an action in Power Automate is a step that performs a specific task within a workflow. It is not the type of operation used to start a workflow based on an external event like adding an item in SharePoint.

The choice "Function Based" is incorrect because Power Automate does not use a function-based approach to start workflows. Triggers and actions are the primary components used to automate processes in Power Automate, and in this case, a trigger is specifically used to start the workflow when an item is added in SharePoint.

explanation: The correct answer is Trigger. Trigger: In Power Automate (formerly known as Microsoft Flow), a "Trigger" is a specific event that initiates a workflow when it occurs. In the scenario described, the new item added to SharePoint serves as the trigger that starts the workflow. Action: While "Action" is an essential part of a workflow, it's not used to initiate the workflow itself. Actions are steps within the workflow that perform specific tasks after the workflow has been triggered. Function-based: "Function-based" is not a commonly used term in the context of triggering workflows in Power Automate. Triggers and actions are the primary building blocks of workflows in Power Automate. Therefore, "Trigger," is the correct choice as it accurately describes the operation used to start a workflow in response to a specific event, such as adding an item in SharePoint. Exam Tip: For the PL-900 exam, focus on: Understanding the difference between triggers and actions. How Power Automate automates business processes using triggers. Best practices for integrating SharePoint with workflows.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A client wants to use Power Platform to improve their business processes, but is worried about connecting it to their custom API, which their operations depend on. How should you respond to reassure them and explain how Power Platform handles this kind of integration?

options.text: The Power Platform offers the ability to create custom connectors for this purpose, which allow you to connect to Power Apps and Power Automate.
options.explanation: Custom connectors in the Power Platform are specifically designed to connect to external systems, including custom APIs. By creating a custom connector, you can define the endpoints, authentication methods, and actions needed to interact with the client's custom API seamlessly within Power Apps and Power Automate. This approach ensures a tailored and efficient integration process. Exam Tip for PL-900 Built-in connectors - Predefined integrations with popular services (SharePoint, Outlook, SQL, Salesforce, etc.). Custom connectors - Bridge external APIs with Power Platform apps when no prebuilt connector exists. Focus on understanding: When to use prebuilt connectors vs. custom connectors. How custom connectors extend Power Platform’s integration capabilities.

options.text: The Power Platform has over 270 connectors to use in these situations.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. While the Power Platform does offer a wide range of pre-built connectors, the availability of over 270 connectors may not guarantee direct compatibility with the client's custom API. In this case, creating a custom connector tailored to the client's specific API requirements would be the most effective approach to ensure a successful integration and meet the client's needs.

options.text: The Power Platform uses connectors that hold a series of functions available for developers.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. While connectors in the Power Platform do provide a series of functions for developers to use, relying solely on existing connectors may not address the unique requirements of the client's custom API. Creating a custom connector allows for greater flexibility and control over the integration process, ensuring a more seamless interaction between the Power Platform and the custom API.

explanation: The correct answer is The Power Platform offers the ability to create custom connectors for this purpose, which allow you to connect to Power Apps and Power Automate. This answer is correct because it addresses the client's concerns directly. Custom connectors can be created in Power Platform, enabling seamless integration with external APIs, including custom ones. It's crucial to grasp why the other choices are incorrect, not just to identify the correct one. This helps enhance your knowledge and decision-making during the exam to eliminate incorrect answers. The Power Platform has over 270 connectors to use in these situations: While it's true that Power Platform offers a wide range of pre-built connectors, this option does not specifically address the client's concern about their custom API. Custom connectors are often needed for unique integration scenarios. The Power Platform uses connectors that hold a series of functions available for developers: This statement is a bit technical and doesn't directly assure the client about the ability to interact with their custom API. It focuses on the technical aspects of connectors rather than addressing the client's concern. How to Create a Custom Connector: Access Power Automate or Power Apps. Navigate to "Custom Connectors" under Data or API settings. Define the API URL, authentication method, and request parameters. Test and deploy the connector for seamless integration. Exam Tip: For the PL-900 exam, focus on: Understanding how custom connectors bridge external APIs with Power Platform apps. The difference between built-in connectors and custom connectors.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A colleague built a model-driven app on Common Data Service to track computer hardware assets and their prices, and worries users might enter wrong values into fields, say, the wrong cost center, when creating a record. How could that be prevented?

options.text: Use Power Automate to validate that the field value matches what the table is expecting.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Using Power Automate to validate field values may help ensure that the data entered matches the expected format or criteria, but it may not specifically address the concern of preventing incorrect values, such as the wrong cost center, from being entered by users.

options.text: Use Business Rules to automatically validate the cost centre for the currently -logged-in user.
options.explanation: Using Business Rules in a model-driven app allows for automatic validation of data based on predefined conditions and actions. By setting up a Business Rule to validate the cost center for the currently logged-in user, you can prevent incorrect values from being entered and ensure data accuracy.

options.text: Use a Canvas App instead of a Model-driven app.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Using a Canvas App instead of a Model-driven app does not directly address the issue of preventing incorrect values from being entered into fields. While Canvas Apps offer flexibility in design and user interface, they do not provide the same level of data validation and automation features as Business Rules in a model-driven app.

explanation: The correct answer is to use Business Rules to automatically validate the cost centre for the currently -logged-in user. Use business rules. Business rules can be used to automate tasks and enforce business logic. For example, you could create a business rule that checks the cost centre field and prevents the record from being saved if the value is not valid. Other ways of preventing this are as follows: Use data validation rules. Data validation rules can be used to restrict the values that can be entered into a field. For example, you could create a rule that only allows numbers to be entered into the cost centre field. Educate users. It is important to educate users about the correct way to use the app. This includes explaining the data validation rules and business rules that are in place. Here are some additional tips: Use clear and concise labels for all fields. Make sure that the field sizes are appropriate for the data that they are collecting. Use a consistent format for all fields. Consider using a color-coding system to highlight incorrect values.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Say your project requires a mobile app where you need complete control over the user experience and design. Which type of Power Apps app should you build to meet that need?

options.explanation: Model Driven Apps are more data-driven and are best suited for scenarios where the data model is complex and needs to be represented in a structured way. They have limited flexibility in terms of design and user experience customization, making them less suitable for scenarios requiring complete control over the user experience and design.

Power Pages are a feature within Power Apps that allows users to create web pages with embedded Power Apps components. While Power Pages offer some design flexibility, they are not specifically designed for building mobile apps and may not provide the level of control over user experience and design required for this scenario.

Canvas Apps provide the most flexibility and control over the user experience and design compared to other types of Power Apps. They allow users to create custom apps with a drag-and-drop interface, enabling full customization of the app's layout, design, and functionality. Canvas Apps are the best choice for building a mobile app where complete control over the user experience and design is a requirement.

explanation: The correct answer is the Canvas App. Key features of Canvas, Model Driven and Power Pages for better understanding. Exam Tips: Focus on: Canvas Apps vs. Model-Driven Apps: Understand their differences and when to use each. Power Automate Basics: Learn how automation enhances business processes. Microsoft Dataverse: Know how it supports data storage and relationships. Power Pages: Know to create sites using power pages. References: Overview of building canvas apps - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn Power Apps model-driven apps documentation - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn What is Power Pages? | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You're building a model-driven app for Vertex Logistics, meant for the Dispatch team to log delivery details. Your instructor, Dr. Kumar, asks: what feature of model-driven apps makes sure they display properly across different devices?

options.explanation: Responsive design is the correct choice as it ensures that model-driven apps can adapt and display appropriately on various devices with different screen sizes and resolutions. This design approach allows the app layout to adjust dynamically to provide an optimal user experience across multiple devices. Key Point for PL-900 Exam Model-driven apps = responsive by default. They automatically adapt to desktop, tablet, and mobile devices without requiring manual layout adjustments. Canvas apps give more control over layout but require manual configuration for responsiveness.

Custom themes do not directly impact how model-driven apps display on different devices. While they can enhance the visual appearance of the app, they do not specifically address the responsiveness of the app layout to accommodate various device sizes and resolutions.

Dynamic layouts can contribute to the flexibility of app design, but they do not solely ensure that model-driven apps display appropriately on different devices. While dynamic layouts can adjust based on certain conditions, they may not fully address the responsiveness needed for diverse device compatibility.

explanation: Responsive design - Model-driven apps automatically adjust to different screen sizes and devices, making them ideal for both desktop and mobile use. Why the others are wrong: Custom themes: Control visual branding, not layout responsiveness. Dynamic layouts: Not a native feature of model-driven apps more applicable to manual UI design in canvas apps. Adaptive algorithms: Sound fancy, but not a real component of Power Apps’ responsiveness.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You're designing a model-driven app for BlueRiver Travel, meant for the Sales team to manage customer bookings. A client, Sophia, asks: what kinds of applications are model-driven apps typically used for?

options.explanation: Model-driven apps are typically used for building business applications that involve data modeling, business processes, and complex data relationships. These apps are well-suited for management applications where structured data and workflows are essential for efficient operations. Key Features of Model-Driven Apps: * Forms - Capture and edit individual records. * Views - Display lists of records with filtering and sorting. * Charts - Provide visual insights into data trends. * Dashboards - Combine multiple components for consolidated analytics. * Responsive design - Automatically adapts to desktop and mobile devices. Exam Tip for PL-900 Model-driven apps = management and operations. They shine in scenarios where structured data, workflows, and analytics are central. Distractors like gaming, social media, and e-commerce highlight use cases that require custom UI or advanced interactivity, which are outside the scope of model-driven apps.

Gaming applications are not typically built using model-driven apps. Model-driven apps are more focused on business processes, data management, and structured workflows rather than entertainment or gaming purposes.

Social media applications usually require a more flexible and dynamic approach to user interactions and content management, which may not align with the structured data modeling and business process automation capabilities of model-driven apps.

E-commerce applications often involve complex product catalogs, customer data, and transaction processing, which can benefit from the data modeling and business logic capabilities of model-driven apps. However, they are not the primary use case for model-driven apps, which are more commonly used for management and business process applications.

explanation: Management applications -  Model-driven apps are commonly used to manage operations like case tracking, customer support, resource scheduling, and analytics dashboards. Why the Other Options Are Wrong Gaming applications Require custom graphics, animations, and complex logic. Model-driven apps are designed for structured data management, not interactive gaming experiences. Social media applications Depend on highly dynamic UIs, real-time feeds, and multimedia features. Model-driven apps focus on structured forms, views, and dashboards, not social networking functionality. E-commerce applications While parts (like product inventory or order tracking) could be built in model-driven apps, full e-commerce solutions demand flexible front-end design and customer-facing features. These are better suited to canvas apps or custom development for rich UI and shopping experiences. References: Explore model-driven app features - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Orion Digital is putting together a new model-driven app for the HR team to manage employee records. The IT team asks: what design approach do model-driven apps follow?

options.explanation: Data-first design is the approach used in model-driven apps where the focus is on designing the data model first before creating the user interface or writing any code. This approach ensures that the data structure and relationships are well-defined and optimized before proceeding with other aspects of app development. Key Exam Insights for PL-900: Model-driven apps = data-first. Canvas apps = UI-first. Power Automate = workflow-first. Low-code principle - Model-driven apps minimize coding, focusing on configuration and leveraging Dataverse

Code-first design is not typically used in model-driven apps as the primary focus is on defining the data model and building the app's functionality through configuration rather than writing custom code. This approach is more common in other types of app development where custom coding is a central part of the design process.

UI-first design is not the approach used in model-driven apps, as the user interface design is typically based on the underlying data model and business logic. While the user interface is important, it is not the starting point for app development in the model-driven approach.

Workflow-first design is not the primary approach in model-driven apps, as workflows and automation are typically built on top of the data model and business logic. While workflows play a crucial role in automating processes within the app, they are not the initial focus in the design process.

explanation:
Data-first design: Model-driven apps prioritize the data model. The structure of your Dataverse tables determines the app’s layout and logic, not the other way around.

Why the Other Options Are Wrong.

Code-first design: Model-driven apps require little to no coding. They emphasize configuration and declarative design over custom development.

UI-first design: This applies to canvas apps, where makers manually design the interface first and then connect data sources. Model-driven apps automatically generate UI based on the data model.

Workflow-first design: More relevant to automation tools like Power Automate. Model-driven apps are not designed around workflows; they are designed around data tables and relationships.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Fill in the blank: ________________ includes apps that integrate into Microsoft 365, Power Apps, and Power Platform services. (Clue: it's the name of a marketplace.)

options.explanation: AppSource is the correct choice as it is Microsoft's marketplace for business applications, including apps that integrate into Microsoft 365, Power Apps, and Power Platform services. It offers a wide range of solutions that can be easily integrated into existing Microsoft products. Keep in Mind: AppSource - Microsoft’s marketplace for business apps that integrate with Microsoft 365, Power BI, Power Apps, and Power Platform. Best for business users seeking plugandplay solutions. Azure Marketplace - Marketplace for IT pros and developers. Focuses on cloud infrastructure solutions like VMs, databases, AI services, and developer tools that run on Azure. Power Automate - A Power Platform service for creating automated workflows. It’s a productivity tool, not a marketplace. Templates and connectors are available, but it doesn’t host thirdparty business apps. Dataverse - The data platform for Power Platform. Provides secure storage, standardized schema, and integration across apps. It’s a backend service, not a marketplace.

Azure Marketplace primarily focuses on offering cloud solutions and services built on the Azure platform. While it may include some applications that integrate with Microsoft products, it is not specifically tailored for apps that integrate into Microsoft 365, Power Apps, and Power Platform services. Exam Tip for PL900 If the question asks about where to find business apps, the correct answer is AppSource. If the question asks about cloud infrastructure solutions, the correct answer is Azure Marketplace. Power Automate and Dataverse are core services in the Power Platform but not marketplaces.

Power Automate is a workflow automation tool within the Power Platform that allows users to automate repetitive tasks and business processes. While it is a part of the Power Platform, it is not specifically related to apps that integrate into Microsoft 365 or Power Apps.

Dataverse, formerly known as Common Data Service, is the data platform within the Power Platform that allows users to securely store and manage data used by business applications. While it is a key component of the Power Platform, it is not directly related to apps that integrate into Microsoft 365 or Power Apps.

explanation: AppSource is Microsoft’s official marketplace for discovering, trying, and acquiring business apps that integrate with Microsoft 365, Power BI, Power Apps, and the rest of the Power Platform. It offers both Microsoft and partner-developed solutions that can enhance workflows, analytics, and overall business productivity. AppSource is intended for business users looking for plug-and-play solutions that work within Microsoft's ecosystem without requiring deep technical setup. Microsoft Marketplace | cloud solutions, AI apps, and agents Azure Marketplace is a marketplace specifically geared toward IT professionals and developers. It offers cloud-based solutions such as virtual machines, databases, machine learning services, and developer tools that are designed to run on Microsoft Azure. While it is similar to AppSource in that it’s a Microsoft marketplace, its focus is on infrastructure and platform solutions, not app integrations with Microsoft 365 or Power Platform. Power Automate is a Power Platform service that helps users create automated workflows between Microsoft services and third-party apps. It is a productivity tool, not a marketplace. While users can browse templates and connectors within Power Automate, it does not provide a catalog of third-party business apps like AppSource does. Instead, it focuses on task automation like sending alerts, moving data, or scheduling activities. Dataverse is the underlying data platform for the Power Platform. It enables secure data storage, standardized data schema, and integration across Power Apps, Power Automate, and other services. It is not a marketplace but rather a backend data service that supports app building and automation. Dataverse helps unify business data, but it doesn’t offer downloadable or installable apps like AppSource.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: At EduTech Academy, the IT team wants to enforce certain rules on their Dataverse tables without writing custom code. What's one of the main advantages of using business rules in Dataverse for this?

options.text: They allow users to enforce logic without custom coding
options.explanation: Business rules in Dataverse allow users to enforce logic without the need for custom coding. This means that non-technical users can easily set up and manage rules to ensure data integrity and consistency within their tables.

options.text: They're only applicable to model-driven apps
options.explanation: Business rules in Dataverse are not limited to model-driven apps only. They can be applied across various types of Power Platform applications, providing flexibility and consistency in enforcing data rules.

options.text: They require Power Fx for implementation
options.explanation: Power Fx is not a requirement for implementing business rules in Dataverse. While Power Fx can be used to create more complex expressions within business rules, basic rule configurations can be set up without the need for Power Fx knowledge.

explanation: Enforcing logic without coding is correct because business rules provide a no-code way to apply logic. Only applicable to model-driven apps is wrong because business rules can apply across Dataverse. Require Power Fx is wrong because business rules don’t need formulas; they’re configured visually.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Fill in the blank: ________________ is the process of proving you're who you say you are, achieved by verifying the identity of a person or device.

options.explanation: Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a person or device, ensuring that they are who they claim to be. It is a crucial step in the security process to prevent unauthorized access to systems or data. Authentication: Logging in with a password. Authorization: Being allowed to view but not edit a file. MFA: Logging in with a password + a code sent to your phone.

This option is incorrect.  Authorization, on the other hand, is the process of determining what actions a user is allowed to perform after they have been authenticated. It defines the level of access and permissions granted to a user or device based on their identity.

This option is incorrect.  Multifactor authentication is a security process that requires multiple forms of verification before granting access. While it enhances security by adding an extra layer of protection, it is not the same as the basic process of proving one's identity, which is authentication.

explanation: Understand the sequence: Always remember authentication comes before authorization. First you prove who you are, then the system checks what you're allowed to do. Focus on the keyword "identity":If the question talks about proving identity, it's authentication. If it talks about accessing resources or permissions, it's authorization. Don't confuse MFA with the process itself: Multifactor Authentication is a security enhancement to authentication, not a standalone identity check. It’s a method, not the definition. Associate examples with each term: Think of real-life scenarios: Authentication: Logging in with a password. Authorization: Being allowed to view but not edit a file. MFA: Logging in with a password + a code sent to your phone.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Still working on that model-driven app for BlueRiver Travel's Sales team to manage customer bookings, Sophia asks: what's the primary data source model-driven apps rely on?

options.explanation: Microsoft Dataverse is the primary data source for model-driven apps in the Microsoft Power Platform. It provides a secure and scalable data platform for storing and managing business data, making it the ideal choice for building model-driven applications. Key Exam Insights for PL-900 Model-driven apps = Dataverse only. Canvas apps = flexible data sources (Dataverse, SharePoint, Excel, SQL, etc.). Power BI = broad data connectivity for analytics. Always remember: Dataverse provides the standardized schema, security, and business rules that model-driven apps depend on.

SQL Server is not the primary data source for model-driven apps in the Microsoft Power Platform. While SQL Server can be integrated with the Power Platform, Microsoft Dataverse is specifically designed to serve as the primary data source for model-driven apps.

Excel spreadsheets are not the primary data source for model-driven apps in the Microsoft Power Platform. While Excel data can be imported and used within the Power Platform, it is not the recommended primary data source for building model-driven applications.

SharePoint lists are not the primary data source for model-driven apps in the Microsoft Power Platform. While SharePoint integration is possible within the Power Platform, Microsoft Dataverse is the preferred data source for model-driven applications due to its robust features and capabilities.

explanation: Microsoft Dataverse -> Model-driven apps are built with a data-first approach and rely exclusively on Dataverse as their data source. Dataverse defines the tables, relationships, and business logic that shape the app’s layout and functionality. Why the others are wrong: SQL Server: While it’s a powerful data source, model-driven apps in Power Platform don't build directly on SQL Server. Excel spreadsheets: More relevant for canvas apps or Power BI not model-driven apps. SharePoint lists: Common for canvas apps, but not valid for building model-driven apps.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A global organization is building a Power Platform solution that connects several business applications, Dataverse, Salesforce, and SQL Server, used across departments. Management wants: users only seeing data relevant to their role; sensitive data never shared with non-approved services; only approved connectors used in production; and environment-level control enforced for makers and admins. Which Power Platform features should be configured to meet all of this? (Select 3)

options.explanation: Security Roles in Dataverse allow organizations to control access to data by defining roles and permissions for different users. By configuring security roles, the organization can ensure that users only access data relevant to their role, thus meeting the requirement of restricting data access based on user roles.

Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Policies in Power Platform help organizations prevent sensitive business data from being shared with non-approved services. By configuring DLP policies, the organization can define rules and actions to protect data and ensure that it is not shared with unauthorized services, meeting the requirement of safeguarding sensitive data.

Environment Roles in Power Platform provide environment-level control for makers and administrators. By assigning specific roles to users within each environment, the organization can enforce control over who can create, modify, and manage resources in the environment, ensuring that only approved connectors are used in production environments.

Solution Checker is not directly related to the requirements mentioned in the question. Solution Checker is a tool that helps makers identify and fix issues in their solutions before deployment, but it does not address the specific requirements of restricting data access, preventing data loss, or enforcing environment-level control.

explanation: A. Security Roles in DataverseSecurity roles define what data users can access and what actions they can perform within Dataverse. This ensures users only see data relevant to their job responsibilities, supporting role-based access control. B. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) PoliciesDLP policies control which connectors can be used together and help prevent sensitive data from being shared with non-approved or risky services like personal or third-party apps. This ensures data compliance and security. C. Environment RolesEnvironment roles control access at the environment level, such as who can be an administrator, maker, or user. This ensures proper governance and limits who can create or manage resources in environments.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You're planning a Power Apps app that needs to read and write data from SharePoint and OneDrive for Business. Which type of app should you build?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect.  Model-driven apps are typically designed for structured data sources such as Microsoft Dataverse (formerly known as the Common Data Service). While they can provide a standardized and structured approach to building apps, they are not specifically designed for working with data from SharePoint and OneDrive for Business. Instead, model-driven apps are ideal when you need to manage and visualize data stored in a centralized, relational database.

Canvas Apps are highly flexible and allow you to build custom applications by designing the user interface (UI) and connecting them to various data sources, including SharePoint and OneDrive for Business. Canvas apps can connect to these data sources using out-of-the-box connectors, enabling users to read and write data. The flexibility of canvas apps makes them an ideal choice for scenarios where you need to access and manipulate data from SharePoint and OneDrive for Business.

This option is incorrect.  Business Process Flows are used to guide users through a series of predefined steps in a process, such as approvals or workflows. While Business Process Flows can help standardize tasks and business processes, they are not designed to read and write data from external sources like SharePoint and OneDrive for Business. Their purpose is to ensure consistency in process execution rather than facilitate data management.

This option is incorrect.  Power Pages is an evolution of Power Apps Portals. It's a platform that allows users to build secure, scalable, and low-code websites that can interact with Microsoft Dataverse and other data sources. Power Pages provides a more refined experience for designing, managing, and deploying external-facing websites. These websites are often used for allowing users outside of an organization (e.g., customers or partners) to interact with business data, submit forms, or access services in a secure and controlled way.

explanation: A canvas app connects to multiple data sources including SharePoint and Excel files stored in OneDrive for Business by using out-of-the-box connectors. Model-driven apps can use only Microsoft Dataverse as the underlying data store. Power Apps portals allow external customers and partners to access data in Microsoft Dataverse. Business process flows are used to standardize business processes, providing a streamlined UI for users to complete a process. Model-driven apps, Power Pages and Business process flows cannot be used to read and write data from SharePoint and OneDrive. Note: Microsoft rebranded Power Apps Portals as Power Pages to better reflect the tool’s capabilities for building websites rather than just portals. The new name emphasizes the web design aspect while still supporting business-centric applications. It is also part of Microsoft's strategy to simplify and streamline the naming of its Power Platform products. References: What is Power Apps and what it can do for you - Training | Microsoft Learn Overview of building canvas apps - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn Overview of building a model-driven app with Power Apps - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A company uses Power Platform, and you need to recommend a use case for formulas in canvas apps. Which TWO actions would you recommend? (Each answer is a complete solution on its own.)

options.explanation: Using formulas in canvas apps to filter a list of rows allows users to dynamically display only the relevant data based on specific criteria. This enhances the user experience by presenting information that is tailored to their needs and improves the app's functionality.

options.text: Save data when a user selects a button.
options.explanation: Formulas in canvas apps can be used to save data when a user selects a button, enabling users to input information and store it in the app or external data sources. This action enhances data management capabilities and allows for interactive user input within the app. Exam Tip for PL-900 FILTER = restrict rows OnSelect = button actions SubmitForm/Patch = save data Formulas ≠ sharing apps

options.text: Change the layout of the app dynamically
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Changing the layout of the app dynamically does not directly relate to the use of formulas in canvas apps. While formulas can be used to manipulate data and control app behavior, they are not typically used for adjusting the visual layout of the app. Formulas are not used to share apps Sharing a canvas app is done through Power Apps Studio or the Power Platform admin center, not via formulas. Formulas are strictly for building and running app logic.

options.text: Grant or revoke access to data sources
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Granting or revoking access to data sources is typically managed through security settings and permissions within the Power Platform environment, rather than through formulas in canvas apps. Formulas are more commonly used for data manipulation and app functionality, rather than controlling data source access.

explanation: FILTER is a common formula used in canvas apps to restrict the rows from a data source or collection. The OnSelect property for a button contains the actions to perform. Formulas such as SubmitForm and Patch are used to save data to a data source. Formulas are not used to share a canvas app. Formulas can only be used when building a canvas app. There is no equivalent formula for the WEBSERVICE Excel function that retrieves XML data from an internet URL. Exam Tips: References: Get started with functions in Power Apps - Training | Microsoft Learn Get started with formulas in canvas apps - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn WEBSERVICE function - Microsoft Support

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A company wants to streamline new-employee onboarding, and needs new hires to manage their active certifications and work history using an Excel workbook. Which Power Apps solution fits this?

options.explanation: Canvas Apps are the most suitable Power Apps solution for allowing users to manage data in an Excel workbook. They provide a flexible and customizable interface that allows users to interact with data in various formats, including Excel. This makes them ideal for streamlining processes like managing certifications and work history for new employees.

This option is incorrect.  Model Driven Apps are more focused on providing a structured and guided user experience based on data models. While they can be used for managing data, they may not offer the same level of flexibility and customization as Canvas Apps when it comes to interacting with Excel workbooks. Therefore, they may not be the best choice for allowing new employees to manage their certifications and work history in an Excel workbook.

This option is incorrect.  Microsoft Dataverse is a database service that provides a secure and scalable storage solution for data used by business applications. While it can be integrated with Power Apps solutions like Canvas Apps and Model Driven Apps, it is not the primary tool for allowing users to directly manage data in an Excel workbook. Therefore, it may not be the most appropriate solution for streamlining the new employee onboarding process in this scenario.

explanation: Canvas Apps are perfect for customizing user experience and connecting to a variety of data sources, including Excel on OneDrive or SharePoint. Model Driven Apps require data stored in Dataverse and are best when business logic and relationships are critical. Microsoft Dataverse is a powerful backend but doesn't directly support Excel as a front-end interface. Exam Tips: Choose Canvas Apps when working with Excel files or non-Dataverse data sources. Remember that Model Driven Apps are tightly coupled with Dataverse. If the scenario involves custom UI and Excel, Canvas Apps are the correct choice. Know the distinction between tools (Apps) and data platforms (like Dataverse). References: What is Power Apps and what it can do for you - Training | Microsoft Learn Build a canvas app - Training | Microsoft Learn Start building apps - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn Create a canvas app with data from an Excel file (contains video) - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You need to build a new model-driven app for a different group of users, and it must restrict which table columns users are allowed to change. Which TWO actions would you take? (Each answer is part of the full solution.)

options.text: A. Configure field-level security for the columns
options.explanation: Configuring field-level security for the columns allows you to restrict access to specific fields within a table. By setting up field-level security, you can control which users or security roles have the ability to view or edit the values in those columns. Exam Tip If the question mentions: Restricting specific columns - Field-level security Restricting table access - Security roles Restricting app behavior - Business rules (but not security)

options.text: B. Assign security roles with appropriate table privileges
options.explanation: Assigning security roles with appropriate table privileges is essential for controlling access to tables within a model-driven app. By assigning security roles with specific privileges, you can ensure that only authorized users have the ability to change values in the restricted columns.

options.text: C. Use Power BI dashboards to control data visibility
options.explanation: Using Power BI dashboards to control data visibility is not directly related to restricting the columns that users can change values in a model-driven app. Power BI dashboards are primarily used for data visualization and analysis, rather than enforcing data editing restrictions.

options.text: D. Create a canvas app instead of a model-driven app
options.explanation: Creating a canvas app instead of a model-driven app does not address the requirement of restricting columns that users can change values. Canvas apps and model-driven apps serve different purposes and have different capabilities, so switching to a canvas app would not solve the issue of column-level restrictions.

options.text: E. Enable Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies
options.explanation: Enabling Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies is important for protecting sensitive data and preventing data leakage, but it does not specifically address the requirement of restricting columns that users can change values in a model-driven app. DLP policies focus on data protection and compliance, rather than granular column-level access control.

explanation: A. Configure field-level security for the columnsField-level security in Microsoft Dataverse is used to restrict access to specific columns in a table. You can control who can read, update, or set values in those columns, making it the correct choice for restricting column-level changes. B. Assign security roles with appropriate table privilegesSecurity roles define table-level permissions such as read, write, create, and delete. Assigning the correct security role ensures users only have the required access to modify data in the model-driven app. Why the other options are incorrect C. Power BI dashboardsPower BI is used for reporting and visualization, not for controlling data modification in apps. D. Create a canvas app instead of a model-driven appChanging the app type does not address column-level security requirements. E. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policiesDLP policies control connector usage and data flow between services, not column-level access inside Dataverse tables.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company plans to transform its business using Power Platform and Dataverse. It needs a central backend solution, connected to Dataverse, that managers and staff can use to manage day-to-day business activities, and it must include process guidance so everyone follows the same procedures. Which solution meets this?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect.  Canvas Apps are used to create custom business applications that connect to your data sources like Dataverse. While Canvas Apps are great for creating custom user interfaces and interactions, they do not provide the structured process guidance required for ensuring everyone follows the same procedures in managing day-to-day activities.

This option is incorrect.  Power Pages are external-facing websites that allow users outside of your organization to interact with your data stored in Dataverse. While Power Pages are useful for external interactions, they do not provide the central backend solution connected to Dataverse that managers and employees need for day-to-day activities management with process guidance. Designed for external users; not suitable as a central backend solution for internal team use with guided processes.

Model Driven Apps are the best choice for creating a central backend solution connected to Dataverse that provides structured process guidance. Model Driven Apps are built on the Dataverse platform and provide a data model-driven user interface, allowing users to easily manage and interact with data while following predefined business processes. This makes Model Driven Apps ideal for ensuring consistency and efficiency in day-to-day business activities.

explanation: Model-driven applications are used to create backend applications connected to Dataverse. They are typically used by management and other employees and can include business process flows for providing guidance to employees. Canvas applications are used to create applications targeted at specific scenarios. Desktop flows are used to create robotic process automations that automate manual tasks typically done by end users. Power Pages sites provide external users access to Dataverse data. They use model-driven application forms and views to display information to external users. References: Describe how to build applications with Microsoft Power Apps - Training | Microsoft Learn Get started with model-driven apps in Power Apps - Training | Microsoft Learn Business process flows overview - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You need a Power Automate flow that lets managers approve or deny vacation requests. Which TWO flow types would work for this? (Each answer is a complete solution on its own.)

options.explanation: Business process flow is the correct choice for creating a Power Automate flow to allow managers to approve or deny vacation requests. It provides a guided user interface to lead users through a defined process, making it ideal for approval workflows like this.

Cloud Flow is the correct choice for creating a Power Automate flow to allow managers to approve or deny vacation requests. Cloud flows are automated workflows that can integrate with various cloud-based services, making them suitable for handling approval processes. Easy Memory Aid Think of flows as how work gets done: Cloud Flows - automation in the cloud (auto, manual, scheduled). Business Process Flows - structured stages for consistency. Desktop Flows - robotic automation for legacy apps. Templates - prebuilt examples to get started.

This option is incorrect.  Instant Flow is not the correct choice for creating a Power Automate flow to allow managers to approve or deny vacation requests. Instant flows are triggered manually by users and are not suitable for automated approval workflows.

This option is incorrect.  Scheduled Flow is not the correct choice for creating a Power Automate flow to allow managers to approve or deny vacation requests. Scheduled flows are triggered at specific times or intervals and are not designed for interactive approval processes like vacation request approvals.

explanation: Business process flows can be used to allow managers to approve or deny vacation requests. Cloud flows can be used to allow managers to approve or deny vacation requests. Desktop flows are used for robotic process automation (RPA). Flow templates are templates, not real flows. Why these two? Business process flows ensure every request follows the same stages and prompts the manager for approval or rejection at the right step. Automated (cloud) flows can watch for new or updated vacation-request records and send out approval cards (via email or Teams) automatically, then update the request based on the manager’s response. Exam Tip: For any approval scenario, pair a business process flow (to enforce the stages and UI guidance) with an automated cloud flow (to handle notifications and update records without manual intervention). References: What is Power Automate and the value it brings to you - Training | Microsoft Learn Overview of the types of flows in Power Automate(contains video) - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power Automate flow that needs to loop through every row in an Excel spreadsheet and update the first column with today's date for each one. Which action would you configure for this?

options.explanation: The "Apply to each" action in Power Automate is specifically designed to iterate over a collection of items, such as rows in an Excel spreadsheet. It allows you to perform actions on each item in the collection, which makes it the ideal choice for looping through all rows in the spreadsheet and updating the first column value for each row with the current date. Key Keywords to Watch For in Exam Questions Apply to each - loop through all items. Do until - loop until condition met. Switch - different actions based on input value. Condition - true/false branching.

This option is incorrect.  The "Condition Action" in Power Automate is used to create conditional logic based on specified criteria. It is not the appropriate action for looping through all rows in an Excel spreadsheet and updating values for each row. This action is more suitable for making decisions based on certain conditions.

This option is incorrect.  The "Switch" action in Power Automate is used to evaluate a single expression against multiple possible values and execute different actions based on the result. It is not designed for looping through rows in an Excel spreadsheet and updating values. This action is more suitable for handling multiple branching scenarios.

This option is incorrect.  The "Do until" action in Power Automate is used to repeatedly execute a set of actions until a specified condition is met. It is not the best choice for looping through all rows in an Excel spreadsheet and updating values for each row with the current date. This action is more appropriate for scenarios where you need to repeat a set of actions until a specific condition is satisfied.

explanation: The Apply to each action allows to loop through items in a collection. In this case, this action can be used to loop through each of the rows in the spreadsheet. Do until allows you to loop through items until a specified condition is met. In this scenario, there is no condition, and every item must be looped through. Switch allows taking an input parameter and performing different steps based on the input’s value. In this case, there are no separate actions to take, but the same action to perform on every single row in the spreadsheet. The condition action allows setting up a conditional statement and then perform an action based on whether the condition is true or false. In this scenario, there is no condition to evaluate since every row must be handled the same way. Exam Tip: In your flow, Use the "List rows present in a table" Excel connector to get the rows, then pass the output to “Apply to each,” and within it. Use the “Update a row” action to write the current date to the first column. References: Exercise - Create recurring flows - Training | Microsoft Learn Use the apply to each action in Power Automate to loop through an array of items. (contains video) - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A company uses Power Automate to integrate applications, and has a legacy application with no API at all. Which type of flow would let you access data inside that legacy app?

options.explanation: Desktop Flows in Power Automate are used to automate repetitive tasks by recording and replaying manual steps on a user's desktop. Since the legacy application does not have an API, Desktop Flows can be used to interact with the application's user interface to access and manipulate data without the need for an API.

This option is incorrect.  An Automated Flow (also known as Scheduled Flow) is designed to trigger based on specific events or on a scheduled basis, and it generally requires the target application to have an accessible API, web service, or a trigger event. Since the legacy application does not have an API, Automated Flows cannot be used to directly access or interact with the application.

This option is incorrect.  An HTTP flow requires the target application to have an API that can be called via an HTTP request. Since the legacy application does not have an API, you cannot use an HTTP flow to directly integrate with it. HTTP flows are designed for services that expose REST APIs or other web services, which isn't the case here.

explanation: Why Desktop Flows? Legacy systems often don’t expose modern APIs or connectors. Desktop Flows use Robotic Process Automation (RPA) to interact with applications through their user interface, mimicking mouse clicks, keyboard input, and reading screen elements. They’re ideal for automating repetitive UI tasks and integrating systems where API integration is not possible. Not suitable: Instant Cloud Flows: Require a trigger and API-based connectors. Scheduled Cloud Flows: Automate tasks based on time, but also rely on API access. Business Process Flows: Guide users through processes in model-driven apps, not for automating legacy system interaction. References: What is Power Automate and the value it brings to you - Training | Microsoft Learn Introduction to desktop flows - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power Automate flow that needs to notify a user every time a new item is added to a SharePoint list, and you need to add an email notification step. What would you use?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect.  Conditions are used to evaluate whether a certain condition is met before executing a specific action in the flow. In this scenario, the requirement is to ensure an email notification is added every time a new item is added to a SharePoint list, which is an action rather than a condition. Condition Definition: Evaluates a true/false statement and branches the flow accordingly. Keyword: If…then Example: “If the request is urgent, send an email; otherwise, do nothing.” Why not here: You want to notify the user every time, so no condition is required.

Actions are the building blocks of a flow that perform specific tasks or operations. In this case, adding an email notification to the flow to notify a user about a new item being added to a SharePoint list is an action that needs to be included in the flow. Action Definition: The step that performs a specific task. Keyword: Does the work Example: “Send an email to notify the user.” Exam Tip: In this scenario, the correct component is an action because the task is to send an email after the trigger. Exam Tip for PL-900 Trigger = starts the flow. Action = performs the task (send email). Condition = only if criteria are met. Apply to each = loop through multiple items. In this case: Trigger (new SharePoint item) - Action (send email).

This option is incorrect.  Triggers are the starting point of a flow and define when the flow should start running based on specific events or conditions. While triggers are essential for initiating the flow, they do not directly relate to adding an email notification to the flow for notifying a user about new items in a SharePoint list. Trigger Definition: Starts the flow when a specific event occurs. Keyword: Starts the flow Example: “When a new item is added to a SharePoint list.” Exam Tip: Triggers initiate but do not perform tasks like sending emails.

This option is incorrect.  Apply to each loops are used to iterate over a collection of items or records and perform the same set of actions for each item. In this scenario, the requirement is to add an email notification for every new item added to a SharePoint list, which does not involve iterating over multiple items. Apply to each loop Definition: Iterates through a collection of items. Keyword: Loop through items Example: “For each row in an Excel table, update the status.” Why not here: There is no collection — just a single new item triggering the flow.

explanation: This item tests the candidate’s knowledge of Power Automate components such as triggers, actions, conditions, and apply to each loop. Action: Actions in Power Automate are the steps that perform specific tasks, like sending an email. In this case, after the trigger (new item added to a SharePoint list), the action you need is to send an email to notify the user. This is an essential part of the flow. Triggers: Triggers are used to start the flow, such as when a new item is added to a SharePoint list. However, triggers do not send email notifications; they only initiate the flow. Condition: A condition would be used if you needed to check whether certain criteria are met before performing a specific task. However, in this scenario, you simply need to notify the user every time a new item is added, so no condition is necessary. Apply to each loop: This loop is used to iterate through a collection of items. Since the task is about notifying the user for each new item (and there is no collection involved), you don't need an "Apply to each" loop in this case. Exam Tips: References: Exercise - Create your first flow - Training | Microsoft Learn Automate tasks by creating a cloud flow - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You need to modify a cloud flow. Which of these approaches could you use to do that?

options.explanation: The Power Automate mobile app enables you to access, monitor, and modify cloud flows on the go. It provides a convenient way to make quick changes and updates to workflows, ensuring your automations stay effective wherever you are. Access on the go: The mobile app lets you view and manage your cloud flows from anywhere. Quick modifications: You can make small edits, enable/disable flows, and adjust settings without needing a desktop. Monitoring: Provides notifications and activity tracking so you can see if flows succeed or fail. Convenience: Ideal for quick updates, approvals, or troubleshooting when you’re away from your workstation. Integration: Works seamlessly with other Microsoft Power Platform tools, keeping your workflows connected across devices.

The Power Automate portal is a web-based platform that enables you to manage and customize cloud flows. It provides a comprehensive set of tools for building, modifying, and optimizing workflows, making it easier to automate processes across your apps and services.

Power Apps Studio is a powerful tool that allows you to create and customize apps that work seamlessly with Power Automate. By using Power Apps Studio, you can integrate your cloud flows with custom applications to enhance their functionality. Power Apps Studio: It is indeed the primary design environment for building and customizing apps in Microsoft Power Apps. Provides a low-code/no-code interface to design screens, controls, and logic. Integration with Power Automate: Power Apps Studio allows you to connect apps with Power Automate cloud flows. This integration lets apps trigger flows (e.g., sending approvals, updating records, sending notifications) directly from user actions. Enhances app functionality by automating processes that go beyond the app itself. Seamless experience: Both tools are part of the Microsoft Power Platform, designed to work together. This makes it easy to extend apps with automation without heavy coding.

This option is incorrect. Copilot Studio is a platform for building AI Agents and Chatbots. While it can integrate with Power Automate to trigger automations, it is not a necessary solution for modifying or managing cloud flows.

explanation: This item tests the candidate’s knowledge of modifying a cloud flow. Power Automate portal – Primary place to edit cloud flows Power Apps Studio – You can open/edit flows created from a canvas app Power Automate mobile app – Allows editing basic flow details and management To modify a cloud flow, the correct tools to use are: Power Automate mobile app: This app allows you to modify cloud flows directly from your mobile device, making it convenient for quick changes while on the go. Power Automate portal: The Power Automate portal is the web-based platform that provides a comprehensive set of tools to create, manage, and modify cloud flows. This is the most robust platform for modifying flows. Power Apps Studio: Power Apps Studio is mainly used for building and customizing apps that interact with Power Automate flows. You can modify a cloud flow that is linked to a Power App via this platform, especially when you need to integrate your flow with custom applications. Explanation of Incorrect Options: Copilot Studio: This tool is used for creating chatbots, and while it can integrate with Power Automate, it is not used for modifying cloud flows. References: How to build an automated solution - Training | Microsoft Learn Create a cloud flow from your phone - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn Understand Power Apps Studio in Dataverse for a Teams environment (contains video) - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: At Horizon Manufacturing, you're building a new app for the Finance team to manage payroll approvals. Your manager, Mr. Carter, stresses the importance of knowing Copilot features, and asks: which of these are actual capabilities of Copilot controls in Power Platform? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Generate app suggestions based on natural language input.
options.explanation: Copilot controls in Microsoft Power Platform can generate app suggestions based on natural language input, making it easier for users to create apps without extensive technical knowledge.

options.text: B. Proposes the best connectors for your scenario (e.g., Outlook, Teams, SharePoint).
options.explanation: Copilot can propose the best connectors for a specific scenario, such as Outlook, Teams, or SharePoint, to streamline the app development process and enhance connectivity.

options.text: C. Provide AI-driven insights and recommendations within apps.
options.explanation: With Copilot controls, users can benefit from AI-driven insights and recommendations within their apps, improving decision-making and overall app functionality.

options.text: D. Enable real-time collaboration between app users.
options.explanation: Copilot enables real-time collaboration between app users, allowing for seamless communication and interaction within the app environment.

options.text: E: Describe the app you want, Copilot generates components.
options.explanation: Copilot controls can describe the app users want, and then generate components based on the description, simplifying the app creation process and saving time.

options.text: AIassisted page creation Copilot can generate entire web pages from natural language prompts (e.g., “Create a customer support page with FAQs and a contact form”).
options.explanation: Copilot offers AI-assisted page creation by generating entire web pages from natural language prompts, such as creating a customer support page with FAQs and a contact form, enhancing the user experience and speeding up development.

explanation: Copilot Capabilities in Power Pages: AIassisted page creation Copilot can generate entire web pages from natural language prompts (e.g., “Create a customer support page with FAQs and a contact form”). Form and data integration It builds forms connected to Dataverse automatically, so site visitors can submit data securely without manual schema setup. Content generation Copilot drafts text for your site, such as product descriptions, help articles, or landing page copy, saving time for makers. Embedded chatbots You can insert conversational AI directly into your site, allowing visitors to ask questions like “What services do you offer?” and get instant answers. Contextual design suggestions While editing, Copilot recommends layouts, themes, or components that fit your site’s purpose (e.g., suggesting a gallery for a portfolio site). Data model alignment Copilot analyzes your Dataverse schema and proposes improvements so your site’s forms and views are optimized for performance. User experience enhancements Visitors can interact with your site through natural language queries instead of clicking through menus (e.g., “Show me upcoming events”). Copilot in Power Apps: Natural Language App Building - Describe the app you want, Copilot generates components. AIPowered Data Suggestions - Recommends tables, relationships, and fields based on your data. Smart Form Creation - Automatically builds forms aligned with your app needs. Embedded AI Chat Control - Adds conversational interfaces inside apps. ContextAware Recommendations - Suggests design or data tips while you build. Data Model Optimization - Analyzes and improves your Dataverse schema. Copilot in Canvas Apps - Helps with formulas, controls, and contextual editing. Query Building Support - Assists in creating queries without coding. AI Responses Embedded in App UI - Users can ask questions like “Show overdue tasks” and get answers directly in the app. Copilot in Power Automate: Workflow Trigger Suggestions - Recommends triggers and actions when setting up flows. Natural Language Flow Creation - Describe the automation you want, Copilot builds the flow. Error Handling Guidance - Suggests conditions, retries, and error paths to make flows more reliable. Connector Recommendations - Proposes the best connectors for your scenario (e.g., Outlook, Teams, SharePoint). Optimization Tips - Identifies redundant steps and suggests simplifications. Data Mapping Assistance - Helps align fields between different systems automatically. Approval Flow Setup - Quickly generates approval workflows with the right actions. Monitoring Insights - Explains flow run results and suggests fixes when failures occur. AIDriven Expressions - Generates Power Automate expressions (e.g., date formatting, calculations) without manual coding. CrossPlatform Integration - Suggests automations that connect Power Apps, Power Pages, and other services.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: NovaTech Systems is building a new app for HR to manage employee onboarding. The IT team asks: when you're learning Power Apps, what data sources are available to you at no extra cost?

options.text: C. Several popular standard data sources
D. None, everything requires a license
