explanation: Correct Answer: D. Automated flow Explanation: Automated flows are triggered by specific events, such as the creation of a new record in Dataverse.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A user wants to see how long each flow takes to run and spot bottlenecks in their automation. Where would they find this performance data?

options.explanation: Power Apps Studio is primarily used for designing and creating Power Apps, not for analyzing flow performance data. It does not provide detailed information on the execution time of flows or bottlenecks in automation processes.

Power Automate run history is the correct choice as it provides detailed information on the execution time of each flow, including start and end times, duration, and any errors encountered during the process. Users can analyze this data to identify bottlenecks and optimize automation processes.

Power BI dashboard is a tool for visualizing and analyzing business data, not specifically designed for tracking flow performance in Power Automate. While Power BI can be used to create custom reports and dashboards, it may not provide the detailed flow execution data needed for performance analysis.

Power Platform Admin Center is more focused on managing and administering the overall Power Platform environment, including user access, security, and governance. While it may provide some high-level insights into flow performance, the detailed execution data and bottleneck analysis are better accessed through the Power Automate run history.

explanation: Correct Answer: B. Power Automate run history Explanation: Run history provides detailed execution times and error logs. Admin Center gives high-level analytics but not step-level timing.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: An organization processes invoices through a legacy desktop application and wants to automate the task without touching the app's code. Which flow type would let them simulate user actions inside that desktop app?

options.explanation: Scheduled flow is not the appropriate choice for simulating user actions in a desktop application as it is designed to run at specific intervals or times without user interaction.
Instant flow is triggered manually by a user or an event, and it does not simulate user actions in a desktop application. It is not suitable for automating tasks in a legacy desktop application.

Desktop flow is the correct choice for simulating user actions in a desktop application without modifying the application's code. It can interact with elements on the screen, input data, and perform tasks just like a user would.
Automated flow is not specifically designed for simulating user actions in a desktop application. It is more focused on automating business processes and workflows within the Power Platform.

explanation:
Correct Answer: C. Desktop flow.

Explanation: Desktop flows use robotic process automation (RPA) to interact with applications that lack APIs by simulating user actions. Some of the use cases of Desktop Flows:

Automated Data Entry into Legacy Applications: Many organizations still rely on legacy desktop or terminal-based applications that don’t have APIs. A desktop flow can mimic human actions (typing, clicking, copying/pasting) to enter or update records automatically.

Invoice Processing: Extract data from PDF invoices or scanned documents. Input the details into ERP or accounting software. Automate repetitive finance tasks without manual intervention.

File and Folder Management: Automate tasks like renaming files, moving them to specific folders, or archiving old records. Useful for HR, finance, or compliance teams that handle large volumes of documents.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company wants to automatically generate documents from Dataverse records. What should they use?

options.explanation: Power BI is a business analytics tool used for visualizing and analyzing data, but it is not specifically designed for document generation from Dataverse records. It is more focused on creating interactive reports and dashboards.

options.text: B. Power Automate with Word templates
options.explanation: Power Automate with Word templates is the correct choice for automating document generation from Dataverse records. Power Automate allows for the creation of automated workflows, and using Word templates enables the generation of documents based on data from Dataverse records.

Power Apps is a platform for building custom business applications, but it is not the ideal choice for automating document generation from Dataverse records. Power Apps is more suited for creating interactive apps with forms and workflows.

explanation: Correct Answer: B. Power Automate with Word templates What is Power Automate + Word Templates? Power Automate: A Microsoft tool that lets you automate repetitive tasks and workflows across Microsoft 365, Dataverse, SharePoint, and many other apps. Word Templates: Pre-designed Word documents with placeholders (also called content controls) that can be dynamically populated with data. Dataverse: A Microsoft data platform that stores structured data (like tables in a database) and integrates seamlessly with Power Automate. How it works together: A Dataverse record is created or updated (e.g., a new customer order). Power Automate detects this event via a trigger. The flow pulls data from the Dataverse record. Data is inserted into the Word template (like filling in placeholders). The completed document can be saved, emailed, or stored automatically

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A logistics company is building a Power Apps mobile solution for warehouse staff that needs to scan items and collect data even when the device has no internet connection. Which of these features support that requirement?

options.text: A. Power BI embedded visuals and cloud flow
options.explanation: Power BI embedded visuals and cloud flow do not directly support the requirement of scanning barcodes, populating product details from Dataverse, working offline, and syncing data when connectivity is restored. These features are more focused on data visualization and automation, rather than the specific functionality needed for this scenario.

options.text: B. Barcode control and offline data collections
options.explanation: Barcode control and offline data collections are the most suitable combination of features to support the requirement. The Barcode control allows users to scan barcodes using mobile devices, while offline data collections enable the app to work without an internet connection and sync data with Dataverse once connectivity is restored. This combination fulfills all the specified requirements effectively. Note: This question is mainly for undertanding how differnt applications within power platform are integrated. Here AI Builder and Canvas Apps.

options.text: C. Power Automate desktop flow and Excel connector
options.explanation: Power Automate desktop flow and Excel connector do not provide the necessary functionality for scanning barcodes, populating product details from Dataverse, working offline, and syncing data when connectivity is restored. These features are more geared towards automation and data manipulation, rather than the specific requirements of this scenario.

options.text: D. Power Pages and SQL Server integration
options.explanation: Power Pages and SQL Server integration do not directly support the requirement of scanning barcodes, populating product details from Dataverse, working offline, and syncing data when connectivity is restored. These features are more focused on data presentation and database integration, rather than the specific functionality needed for this scenario.

explanation: Correct Answer: B. Barcode control and offline data collections Explanation: Canvas apps support barcode scanning using the Barcode control. Offline data collections allow temporary storage of scanned data, which can be synced with Dataverse when the device reconnects.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: At Evergreen Foods, building an app for Procurement to track supplier invoices, your manager Mr. Daniels stresses the importance of branding and asks: in Power Pages, if you want to change your site's look and feel by adjusting its theme, which option lets you do that?

options.text: A. Use the Theme workspace in the Power Pages design studio to adjust branding elements like colors and fonts.
options.explanation: Using the Theme workspace in the Power Pages design studio is the correct option to adjust branding elements like colors and fonts. This workspace allows you to customize the look and feel of your site by modifying the theme settings, such as color schemes, fonts, and other visual elements.

options.text: B. Modify the Dataverse schema to apply a new theme across all tables and forms.
options.explanation: Modifying the Dataverse schema does not directly apply a new theme to Power Pages. The Dataverse schema is used for defining and organizing data within the Power Platform, and it is not related to changing the visual appearance of a site through theme customization.

options.text: C. Edit the portal management app’s security roles to unlock hidden theme customization features.
options.explanation: Editing the portal management app's security roles does not unlock hidden theme customization features in Power Pages. Security roles are used to control access and permissions within the portal management app, and they do not have a direct impact on modifying the site's theme.

options.text: D. Configure environment variables in Power Platform Admin Center to override the default site theme globally.
options.explanation: Configuring environment variables in Power Platform Admin Center to override the default site theme globally is not the correct option for changing the look and feel of a site in Power Pages. Environment variables are used for managing configuration settings and parameters across different environments, but they do not control the visual appearance of a site through theme customization.

explanation: As per the study guide, you need to know the below: What is a Power Pages Theme? A theme in Power Pages controls the look and feel of your site - including colors, fonts, button styles, and overall branding. It ensures your site matches your organization’s identity and provides a consistent user experience. How to Modify a Power Pages Theme Open the Design Studio Go to your Power Pages site in the Power Pages design studio. Select the site you want to customize. Navigate to the Theme Workspace In the left-hand panel, choose Theme. This workspace allows you to adjust branding elements without writing code. Customize Branding Elements Colors: Change primary, secondary, and background colors to match your company’s palette. Fonts: Select typography styles for headings, body text, and buttons. Buttons & Links: Adjust styles for hover effects, borders, and text alignment. Layouts: Apply consistent spacing and alignment across pages. Preview Changes Use the preview mode to see how your changes look before publishing. This ensures the theme aligns with your brand guidelines. Publish the Theme Once satisfied, click Publish to apply the theme across your site. All pages will automatically reflect the updated design. Why Modify a Theme? Brand Consistency: Aligns your site with corporate branding. User Experience: Improves readability and navigation. Professional Appearance: Makes your site look polished and trustworthy. Flexibility: Allows quick changes without editing CSS or HTML manually. Study guide for Exam PL-900: Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals | Microsoft Learn

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: A company has built an agent in Copilot Studio and is getting ready to make it available to both employees and customers. The project manager is walking the team through how channels work. Which of these statements about Copilot Studio channels are true? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Channels determine where users can access an agent.
options.explanation: Channels in Copilot Studio determine the platforms or locations where users can interact with the agent. By defining channels, the company can control where the agent is accessible to users, such as through a website, mobile app, or messaging platform.

options.text: B. An agent can be published to multiple channels.
options.explanation: An agent in Copilot Studio can be published to multiple channels simultaneously. This allows the company to reach a wider audience by making the agent available on various platforms or communication channels.

options.text: C. Microsoft Teams is a supported channel.
options.explanation: Microsoft Teams is a supported channel in Copilot Studio, meaning that the agent can be integrated and accessed within the Microsoft Teams platform. This expands the reach of the agent to users who utilize Microsoft Teams for communication and collaboration.

Channels in Copilot Studio do not define conversation topics. Conversation topics are typically defined within the agent's design and configuration, while channels determine where and how users can engage with the agent.

Channels in Copilot Studio are primarily focused on determining the access points for users to interact with the agent and do not provide business data. Business data is typically managed and utilized within the agent's logic and integration with other systems, separate from the concept of channels.

explanation: Channels specify where users interact with the agent (Teams, websites, etc.). Agents can indeed be published to multiple channels simultaneously. Microsoft Teams is one of the supported channels. Channels do not define conversation topics - that’s handled by Topics. Channels do not provide business data - that comes from Dataverse tables or knowledge sources.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: The Power Pages design studio provides several workspaces for building and managing sites. Which of these correctly describe those workspaces? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Pages workspace - used to create and edit site pages, add text, images, and forms.
options.explanation: The Pages workspace in Power Pages is where users can create and edit site pages, add various elements such as text, images, and forms to design the layout and content of the site.

options.text: B. Data workspace - connects to Dataverse tables and manages data integration for the site.
options.explanation: The Data workspace in Power Pages allows users to connect to Dataverse tables and manage data integration for the site. It enables users to handle data effectively and ensure seamless data flow within the site.

options.text: C. Theme workspace - customizes branding elements such as colors, fonts, and styles.
options.explanation: The Theme workspace in Power Pages is dedicated to customizing branding elements like colors, fonts, and styles. Users can create a unique and cohesive visual identity for their site by adjusting these design elements.

options.text: D. Setup workspace - configures authentication, security, and site settings.
options.explanation: The Setup workspace in Power Pages is where users can configure authentication settings, manage security measures, and adjust site settings to ensure the site operates securely and efficiently. This workspace is crucial for setting up the foundational aspects of the site.

explanation: Check out the detailed documentation on Power Pages: Create an AI-generated web page using Copilot | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're designing an app for Skyline Airlines' Scheduling team to manage crew rosters. A client, Rachel, asks: in Power Automate cloud flows, which statement best describes how loops and branching are used?

options.text: A. Loops allow you to repeat actions for each item in a collection, while branching enables conditional execution of actions based on logical expressions.
options.explanation: Loops in Power Automate cloud flows allow you to iterate over each item in a collection, enabling you to repeat actions for each item. On the other hand, branching enables conditional execution of actions based on logical expressions, allowing you to create different paths for the flow to follow based on specified conditions.

options.text: B. Loops are only available in desktop flows, and branching requires custom code.
options.explanation: Loops are not limited to desktop flows; they are also available in cloud flows. Branching in Power Automate does not require custom code; it allows you to create conditional paths based on logical expressions without the need for coding.

options.text: C. Loops automatically run actions in parallel without configuration, and branching always requires approval steps.
options.explanation: Loops in Power Automate cloud flows do not automatically run actions in parallel without configuration. They iterate over items sequentially. Branching does not always require approval steps; it allows you to create conditional paths based on logical expressions without the need for approvals.

options.text: D. Loops and branching cannot be combined in the same cloud flow.
options.explanation: Loops and branching can be combined in the same Power Automate cloud flow. Loops can iterate over items in a collection, while branching allows for conditional execution of actions based on logical expressions, enabling a combination of repetitive and conditional actions within the same flow.

explanation: Loops (Apply to each, Do until): Used to repeat actions for multiple items, such as processing each record in a list. Branching (Condition, Switch): Used to control flow logic, e.g., “If stock < 10, send email; else update record.” Both can be combined in the same flow to build complex automation scenarios.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: As an app maker at CrystalWave Media building an app for IT to track support escalations, your manager Ms. Johnson asks: in Power Automate Desktop flows, what are 'actions'?

options.text: A. Pre-built automation steps that interact with applications, files, and systems (e.g., clicks, keystrokes, data extraction).
options.explanation: In Power Automate Desktop flows, "actions" refer to pre-built automation steps that allow users to interact with various applications, files, and systems. These actions can include clicking, keystroking, data extraction, and other automated tasks without the need for manual coding.

options.text: B. Custom scripts that must be manually coded in languages like Python or JavaScript.
options.explanation: Custom scripts that require manual coding in languages like Python or JavaScript are not considered "actions" in Power Automate Desktop flows. Actions are predefined automation steps that simplify the process of creating automated workflows.

options.text: C. Cloud-only connectors used to integrate services such as Outlook, SharePoint, or Teams.
options.explanation: Cloud-only connectors used to integrate services like Outlook, SharePoint, or Teams are not categorized as "actions" in Power Automate Desktop flows. Actions specifically refer to pre-built automation steps within the Power Automate Desktop environment.

options.text: D. Administrative settings that define user permissions and security roles for running flows.
options.explanation: Administrative settings that define user permissions and security roles for running flows are not referred to as "actions" in Power Automate Desktop flows. Actions are focused on the automation steps within the workflow, rather than the administrative settings related to user permissions.

explanation: Notice how B, C, and D are plausible-sounding but incorrect: B confuses actions with coding, but desktop flows are low-code/no-code. C applies to cloud flows, not desktop flows. D refers to governance/security, not automation steps. This is part of the study guide under the topic - Describe actions for Power Automate desktop flows Study guide for Exam PL-900: Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Leo mentions the app being built for Marketing to measure campaign ROI, and says he's heard Copilot can simplify site creation. Maya asks: when using Copilot in Power Pages to create or modify a site, which of these capabilities are actually supported? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Generate site pages and layouts by describing them in natural language prompts.
options.explanation: Copilot in Power Pages allows users to generate site pages and layouts by describing them in natural language prompts. This feature simplifies the process of creating or modifying a site by providing a more intuitive way to communicate design requirements.

options.text: B. Automatically configure Dataverse tables and forms without any manual setup.
options.explanation: Copilot in Power Pages does not automatically configure Dataverse tables and forms without any manual setup. This capability is not supported by Copilot, as it focuses on assisting with site design and content creation rather than database configuration.

options.text: C. Suggest themes, styles, and branding elements based on your description.
options.explanation: Copilot in Power Pages can suggest themes, styles, and branding elements based on the user's description. This feature helps streamline the design process by providing recommendations for visual elements that align with the user's preferences and requirements.

options.text: D. Provide guided assistance to edit existing site content, such as text or navigation.
options.explanation: Copilot in Power Pages offers guided assistance to edit existing site content, such as text or navigation. This feature helps users make quick edits and updates to their site content with the help of contextual guidance and suggestions.

explanation: A. Generate site pages and layouts: Copilot can create new pages by interpreting natural language instructions. B. Configure Dataverse tables automatically: While Copilot can assist with connecting data, full table configuration still requires manual setup in the Data workspace. C. Suggest themes and styles: Copilot can recommend branding elements like colors and fonts to match your description. D. Edit existing content: Copilot helps modify text, navigation, and layouts interactively. This is part of the study guide under the topic - Create and modify Power Pages sites by using Copilot Study guide for Exam PL-900: Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: At Evergreen Foods, building an app for Procurement to track supplier invoices, your manager Mr. Daniels stresses data protection and asks: which of these best describe key security concepts in Power Pages? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Security is managed through web roles, which define what authenticated and anonymous users can access.
options.explanation: Security in Power Pages is primarily managed through web roles, which define the access levels for both authenticated and anonymous users. These roles determine what specific actions users can perform and what data they can access within the Power Platform environment.

options.text: B. Table permissions control access to Dataverse data displayed in forms and lists.
options.explanation: Table permissions play a crucial role in controlling access to Dataverse data that is displayed in forms and lists within Power Pages. By setting up appropriate permissions at the table level, administrators can ensure that only authorized users can view or modify specific data.

options.text: C. Authentication providers (e.g., Azure AD, LinkedIn) can be configured to manage how users sign in.
options.explanation: Authentication providers such as Azure AD and LinkedIn can be configured within Power Pages to manage how users sign in to the platform. By integrating these authentication providers, administrators can enforce secure sign-in processes and control user access based on their identity.

options.text: D. Theme workspace settings determine which users can view or edit secure content.
options.explanation: Theme workspace settings are not directly related to key security concepts in Power Pages. These settings primarily determine the visual appearance and layout of the workspace, rather than controlling user access or permissions to secure content.

explanation: Quick Summary Web Roles = Who can access pages Table Permissions = What data they can use Authentication Providers = How they log in Theme Workspace = How the site looks Web Roles (A) Web roles are used to decide what a user is allowed to see or do on the website. Simple meaning: They control access to pages, forms, and lists for different users or groups. Example:A customer may only see their own data, while an admin can see everything. Table Permissions (B) Table permissions control what users can do with data in Dataverse. Simple meaning: They decide if a user can create, read, update, or delete records. Example:A user may be allowed to view complaints but not delete them. Authentication Providers (C) Authentication providers control how users log in to the Power Pages site. Simple meaning: They manage sign-in options like Microsoft, Google, or external accounts. Example:A customer logs in using their Google or Microsoft account. Theme Workspace (D) Theme workspace is used for design and appearance only. Simple meaning: It changes how the website looks (colors, fonts, style), not security. Example: Making the site look branded with company colors. This is part of the study guide under the topic - Describe Power Pages security concepts Study guide for Exam PL-900: Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: At BrightLine Insurance, building an app for Customer Service to log policyholder claims, Mr. Carter raises a question in a review meeting: in Power Platform, what does process mining primarily help organizations achieve? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Analyze and visualize how business processes are actually executed based on system event logs.
options.explanation: Process Mining in Power Platform primarily helps organizations analyze and visualize how business processes are actually executed based on system event logs. By doing so, organizations can gain insights into their processes, identify areas for improvement, and make data-driven decisions to optimize their operations.

options.text: B. Automatically generate new applications without user input.
options.explanation: Generating new applications without user input is not the primary purpose of Process Mining in Power Platform. Process Mining focuses on analyzing and improving existing business processes based on event logs, rather than creating new applications automatically.

options.text: C. Identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and opportunities for automation in workflows.
options.explanation: Process Mining in Power Platform is used to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, and opportunities for automation in workflows. By analyzing process data, organizations can streamline their operations, automate repetitive tasks, and enhance overall efficiency.

options.text: D. Replace all manual tasks with robotic process automation (RPA) instantly.
options.explanation: While robotic process automation (RPA) can be a part of process automation initiatives, Process Mining in Power Platform does not aim to replace all manual tasks with RPA instantly. The primary goal is to analyze and optimize existing processes based on data insights, rather than automating all tasks without consideration.

explanation: Process Mining in Power Automate uses event logs and system data to reconstruct how processes are executed in reality, not just how they are designed. It provides visual maps of workflows, showing steps, variations, and performance metrics. The main value is to identify bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and areas where automation or optimization can improve outcomes. Option B is incorrect because process mining doesn’t automatically generate apps. Option D is misleading - while process mining can inform automation, it doesn’t instantly replace all manual tasks. This question is part of the study guide under the topic Describe Process Mining. References: Overview of process mining in Power Automate - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn Study guide for Exam PL-900: Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals | Microsoft Learn

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: A company has already built and tested an agent. What's the next step to actually make it available to users?

options.explanation: Creating topics is not the next step to make the agent available to users. Topics are used to organize conversations and manage the flow of communication within the agent, but they do not directly impact the availability of the agent to users.

Configuring knowledge sources is important for training the agent and improving its performance, but it is not the immediate next step to make the agent available to users. Knowledge sources help the agent provide accurate and relevant responses, but publishing the agent is necessary for users to interact with it.

options.text: C. Publish the agent by using a channel
options.explanation: Publishing the agent by using a channel is the correct next step to make the agent available to users. By publishing the agent through a channel, such as a website or messaging platform, users can access and interact with the agent to receive assistance or information.

Creating Dataverse tables is not directly related to making the agent available to users. Dataverse tables are used for storing data within the Power Platform environment and are not a necessary step in the process of deploying and enabling user access to the agent.

explanation: Once an agent has already been built and tested, the next step to make it available to users is to publish the agent by using a channel. Here’s why the other options don’t fit at this stage: Create Topics: This is part of designing the agent’s conversation flow, not the step for making it available. Configure Knowledge Sources: This enhances the agent’s ability to answer questions, but it’s still internal setup. Create Dataverse tables: Useful for storing structured data, but not required for publishing. Publish the agent by using a channel: This is the deployment step - connecting the agent to a channel like Microsoft Teams, a website, or another platform so users can interact with it.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You want to build a canvas app using Copilot to speed up development. What's the first step you need to take to make sure Copilot can properly generate the Dataverse tables your app needs?

options.text: A. Ensure that the app's design is finalized before involving Copilot
options.explanation: Finalizing the app's design before involving Copilot is not a necessary step to ensure Copilot can effectively generate the necessary Dataverse tables. Copilot can assist in the design and development process, so having a finalized design beforehand is not a prerequisite for its functionality.

options.text: B. Provide a clear and concise description of the app's purpose and data requirements
options.explanation: Providing a clear and concise description of the app's purpose and data requirements is crucial for Copilot to effectively generate the necessary Dataverse tables. By clearly outlining the app's objectives and data needs, Copilot can better understand the app's structure and generate the appropriate tables accordingly.

options.text: C. Manually create all Dataverse tables before using Copilot
options.explanation: Manually creating all Dataverse tables before using Copilot is not required as Copilot is designed to assist in generating tables based on the app's requirements. Manually creating tables beforehand may not align with the app's actual needs and could lead to unnecessary duplication of effort.

explanation: Correct Answer: B. Provide a clear and concise description of the app's purpose and data requirements Why right: Copilot relies on natural language prompts to generate Dataverse tables correctly. Why wrong: A. Finalizing design before Copilot - Wrong because Copilot helps during design, not after. C. Manually creating tables - Wrong because Copilot can generate them automatically.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Which of these statements about canvas apps and model-driven apps is FALSE?

options.text: Canvas apps allow makers to design the user interface freely by dragging and dropping controls.
Model-driven apps automatically generate user interfaces based on Dataverse tables and relationships.
Canvas apps can connect to multiple data sources, including Dataverse, SharePoint, and SQL.
Model-driven apps are best suited for complex business processes that rely heavily on structured data.
Canvas apps provide pixel-perfect control over layout, while model-driven apps follow a standardized UI.
Model-driven apps cannot use Dataverse as a data source.

Canvas apps indeed allow makers to design the user interface freely by dragging and dropping controls, providing a flexible and customizable UI design experience. The second statement is True. Model-driven apps automatically generate user interfaces based on Dataverse tables and relationships, simplifying the UI creation process for structured data. The third statement is True. section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Which of these statements about Power Platform security is FALSE?

options.text: Multifactor authentication (MFA) strengthens security by requiring verification beyond just a password.
Role-based access control (RBAC) ensures users only have permissions appropriate to their assigned role.
Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies restrict data flow between business and non-business connectors.
Encryption at rest protects stored data from unauthorized access.
Conditional access policies let administrators enforce rules about when and how users can log in.
Role-based access control (RBAC) is used to encrypt data during transfer between connectors.

explanation: All statements are true except for the last one, which states that Role-based access control (RBAC) is used to encrypt data during transfer between connectors. RBAC is primarily focused on managing user permissions based on roles, not on encryption during data transfer.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: At GlobalCorp, admins are planning strict governance across multiple Power Platform environments, sensitive data needs to stay isolated, lifecycle management needs to stay consistent, and developers need to be able to test without touching production. Which combination of environment types and features best supports this?

options.text: A. Use Production environments for live apps, Sandbox environments for testing, and enforce Managed Environments for governance.
options.explanation: Using Production environments for live apps ensures that sensitive data is isolated and lifecycle management is consistent. Sandbox environments are ideal for testing without impacting production, and enforcing Managed Environments adds an extra layer of governance to maintain control and security.

options.text: B. Use Trial environments for sensitive data, Default environment for production, and rely on Conditional Access for governance.
options.explanation: Trial environments are not suitable for sensitive data as they are temporary and not intended for long-term use. Default environments may not provide the necessary level of security and governance required for strict governance. Conditional Access is more focused on controlling access to resources rather than governance across Power Platform environments.

options.text: C. Use Developer environments for production workloads, Sandbox environments for governance, and Data Loss Prevention policies for testing.
options.explanation: Developer environments are typically used for development and testing purposes, not for production workloads. Sandbox environments are more appropriate for governance and testing, but using them for production workloads can lead to inconsistencies and security risks. Data Loss Prevention policies are more focused on preventing data loss rather than overall governance.

options.text: D. Use Microsoft Dataverse for Teams environments for enterprise apps, Production environments for testing, and Encryption at Rest for governance.
options.explanation: Microsoft Dataverse for Teams environments are more suitable for collaboration within Microsoft Teams, not for enterprise apps that require strict governance. Using Production environments for testing can lead to potential disruptions in live apps. Encryption at Rest is a security feature that focuses on data protection rather than overall governance across Power Platform environments.

explanation: A. Production + Sandbox + Managed Environments Production environments are designed for longterm, stable use with live data and businesscritical apps. They ensure sensitive data is properly isolated and governed. Sandbox environments provide a safe space for testing and development without affecting production data. They allow developers to validate changes before deployment. Managed Environments add governance features like monitoring, sharing controls, and compliance enforcement across environments. This ensures consistent lifecycle management and organizational oversight. Together, this combination directly addresses the scenario: isolation of sensitive data, structured ALM, and safe testing. Why others are wrong: B. Trial + Default + Conditional Access Trial environments are temporary and not suitable for sensitive data storage. Default environment is shared by all users and not intended for production workloads. Conditional Access enforces login rules but does not provide governance across environments. C. Developer + Sandbox + DLP Developer environments are for individual makers under a Developer Plan, not for production workloads. Sandbox environments are for testing, not governance. DLP policies control connector data flow, not testing or lifecycle governance. D. Dataverse for Teams + Production + Encryption at Rest Dataverse for Teams environments are lightweight and tied to Teams, not suitable for enterprise apps. Production environments are for live apps, not testing. Encryption at Rest

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A developer has built a cloud flow in Power Automate and wants to confirm it works correctly before sharing it with users. Which of these are valid ways to test a cloud flow? (Select all that apply)

options.text: a) Run the flow manually using the Test option in Power Automate
options.explanation: Running the flow manually using the Test option in Power Automate allows the developer to simulate the flow's execution and verify its functionality before sharing it with users. This helps in identifying any potential issues or errors that need to be addressed.

options.text: b) Use sample data or previous run data during testing
options.explanation: Using sample data or previous run data during testing provides the developer with the ability to test the flow with different scenarios and inputs. This helps in ensuring that the flow behaves as expected under various conditions before it is shared with users.

options.text: c) Deploy the flow to production without testing
options.explanation: Reviewing the run history to check success and failure details allows the developer to analyze the past executions of the flow. This helps in identifying any patterns of success or failure, debugging issues, and making necessary improvements to the flow before sharing it with users.

options.text: d) Review run history to check success and failure details
options.explanation: Deploying the flow to production without testing is not a valid way to ensure the flow works correctly. Testing is essential to identify and resolve any issues or errors before making the flow available to users in a production environment.

options.text: e) Use debugging features to step through each action in real time
options.explanation: Using debugging features to step through each action in real time can be a helpful way to troubleshoot and identify any issues in the flow's execution. This allows the developer to pinpoint specific areas of concern and make necessary adjustments for optimal performance before sharing the flow with users.

explanation: Testing a cloud flow includes: Running the flow manually (Test option) Using sample or real trigger data Checking run history for results and errors

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company is weighing Dataverse against a traditional SQL database for building Power Platform business apps. Which of these correctly describe an advantage Dataverse has over a traditional database? (Select all that apply)

options.text: a) Dataverse provides built-in integration with Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI
options.explanation: Dataverse provides seamless integration with Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI, allowing for a more streamlined development and data visualization process within the Power Platform ecosystem. This integration simplifies data sharing and automation tasks, enhancing the overall user experience.

options.text: b) Dataverse requires only SQL queries and no low-code tools for usage
options.explanation: Dataverse does not solely rely on SQL queries; it offers a low-code environment that enables users to build and customize business applications without extensive coding knowledge. This feature makes Dataverse more accessible and user-friendly compared to traditional databases that may require advanced SQL skills.

options.text: c) Dataverse includes built-in role-based security and business rules
options.explanation: Dataverse comes with built-in role-based security and business rules, which help in enforcing data access controls and maintaining data integrity. This feature enhances data security and governance, ensuring that only authorized users can access and manipulate data within the platform.

options.text: d) Traditional databases are always easier to use than Dataverse for business users
options.explanation: Dataverse is a managed platform, meaning that Microsoft handles the infrastructure management tasks such as maintenance, updates, and scalability. This reduces the burden on IT teams and allows organizations to focus more on building and optimizing their business applications rather than managing the underlying infrastructure.

options.text: e) Dataverse is a managed platform that reduces infrastructure management effort
options.explanation: Traditional databases may be familiar to some users, but Dataverse offers advantages such as integrated Power Platform services, built-in security features, and managed infrastructure that make it a compelling choice for building business applications. While there may be a learning curve for transitioning from traditional databases to Dataverse, the benefits it provides outweigh the perceived ease of use of traditional databases.

explanation: Dataverse advantages: Native Power Platform integration Built-in security and business logic Low-code development Managed service (less maintenance) Resources

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A company wants to see how its purchase-approval process actually plays out in real life, spot delays, and improve efficiency using Power Platform. Which feature best supports this?

options.text: a) Power BI dashboards for reporting sales data
options.explanation: Power BI dashboards are primarily used for reporting and visualizing sales data, not for analyzing and improving business processes like the purchase approval process. While Power BI can provide valuable insights into sales performance, it is not the best feature for analyzing process efficiency and identifying delays in the purchase approval process.

options.text: b) Process mining in Power Automate
options.explanation: Process mining in Power Automate is the best feature to support the company's requirement of analyzing the purchase approval process, identifying delays, and improving efficiency. Process mining allows organizations to visualize and analyze their business processes, identify bottlenecks, and optimize workflows for improved efficiency. It is specifically designed for process analysis and improvement, making it the most suitable choice for the company's needs.

options.text: c) Power Pages web templates for external websites
options.explanation: Power Pages web templates are used for creating external websites and web content, not for analyzing and improving internal business processes like the purchase approval process. While Power Pages can be useful for external-facing content, they do not provide the functionality needed to analyze process efficiency and identify delays within the company's internal processes.

options.text: d) Dataverse table relationships for data storage
options.explanation: Dataverse table relationships are used for defining data relationships and storing data within the Dataverse environment. While data storage and relationships are important for analyzing processes, Dataverse table relationships alone do not provide the process analysis and optimization capabilities required to analyze the purchase approval process, identify delays, and improve efficiency. Process mining in Power Automate is better suited for this specific requirement.

explanation: Process mining: Analyzes real business process data from systems Shows how processes actually flow (not just how they are designed) Identifies bottlenecks, delays, and inefficiencies Helps improve and optimize workflows Resources

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A company uses Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and an on-premises SQL database. Employees currently submit expense claims by email, which causes delays and missed approvals. The company wants a solution that: lets employees submit claims from mobile devices; automatically routes approvals to managers; stores approved claims in the SQL database; sends notifications in Teams; and needs minimal custom code. Which combination of Power Platform tools should be used?

options.explanation: Power BI is a business analytics tool used for visualizing and analyzing data, while Dataverse is a data platform that allows you to securely store and manage data used by business applications. Although Power BI can help with data visualization, it does not provide the functionality needed to create a solution for expense claim submission, approval routing, and storage in an SQL database.

Power Apps is a low-code application development platform that allows you to create custom business apps, while Power Automate is a workflow automation tool that can automate the process of routing approvals and sending notifications. This combination of tools can be used to create a solution for expense claim submission, approval routing, storage in an SQL database, and sending notifications in Microsoft Teams, all with minimal custom code.

AI Builder is a tool that allows you to add AI capabilities to your applications, such as image recognition or text analysis. While AI Builder can enhance the functionality of your solution, it does not provide the core capabilities needed to create a solution for expense claim submission, approval routing, and storage in an SQL database.

explanation: Power Apps is best for creating the mobile-friendly expense submission application. Power Automate handles approval workflows, SQL storage, and Teams notifications with low-code automation capabilities.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Fill in the blank: a business process flow can have no more than ________________ stages.
explanation: Keep in Mind on Limitations: This might change time to time as MS Updates time to time. Pls refer to the MS Learning paths to know about the latest limitations. This question is purely for information purpose to understand the limitations. This will help you when you build flows. General Power Platform Limits 1) How many API requests can a user make per day? API request limits vary by license. For example, Microsoft 365 users typically get 6,000 requests per 24 hours, while premium licenses offer more. 2) What happens if a flow exceeds its request limits? Flows may be throttled or turned off if they exceed limits continuously for 14 days. Power Automate Limits 1) How many actions can a single flow contain? A flow can have up to 500 actions. Exceeding this may cause performance issues. 2) What is the maximum nesting depth for actions? You can nest actions up to 8 levels deep, such as within conditions or switch cases. 3) How many switch cases are allowed in a flow? A single switch scope can contain up to 25 cases. 4) How many variables can be used in a flow? Each flow can include up to 250 variables. 5) How many flows can a single user own? A user can own up to 600 cloud flows in one environment. 6) What is the maximum run duration for a flow? Flows can run for up to 30 days before being automatically stopped. 7) How long are flow run histories retained? Run data is retained for 30 days from the start time. 8) What happens to dormant flows? Flows not triggered for 90 days may be turned off, especially under Free, Trial, or Microsoft 365 plans. Dataverse Limits 1) How many active business process flows are allowed per table? Each Dataverse table can have up to 10 active business process flows. 2) How many stages can each business process flow contain? Each flow can include up to 30 stages. Environment Limits 1) Is there a limit to the number of environments in Power Platform? There’s no fixed cap, but Dataverse for Teams may have practical limits. Regular environments are constrained by storage capacity, not a hard number. References https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/learn/modules/build-automated-solution/4-build-business-process-flow https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/business-process-flows-overview

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: A company wants to test an agent with a small group of users before rolling it out to customers. Which channel should be used first?

options.explanation: A Demo Website is the most suitable channel for testing an agent with a small group of users before making it available to customers. It provides a controlled environment where the agent can be tested and refined without the risk of exposing it to a wider audience prematurely.

Microsoft Teams is a collaboration platform that may not be the best choice for testing an agent with a small group of users. While it can be used for internal communication and collaboration, it may not provide the necessary controlled environment for testing the agent before releasing it to customers.

Facebook is a social media platform that is more suited for reaching a wider audience, including customers, rather than testing an agent with a small group of users. Using Facebook as the first channel may expose the agent to a larger audience before it has been adequately tested.

Direct Line is a channel that allows for direct communication with the agent, but it may not be the best choice for testing with a small group of users. Direct Line is more suitable for providing direct access to the agent for customers, rather than for initial testing and refinement with a limited user group.

explanation: Microsoft Teams: Ideal for internal pilots. It allows controlled access, easy feedback collection, and collaboration among employees or test users before rolling out to external customers. Demo Website: Useful for showcasing functionality, but less effective for gathering structured feedback from a small group. Facebook: Too public for early testing; better suited for customer-facing launches. Direct Line: Provides integration flexibility but requires more development effort, making it less practical for initial small-scale testing.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: During a training workshop at NovaTech, the facilitator poses this to participants, true or false: after creating a user-owned custom entity in Dataverse, you can change its ownership from user-owned to organization-owned.

options.explanation: This is incorrect option.  In Common Data Service (CDS), now part of Microsoft Dataverse, when you create a custom entity, you must specify its ownership type: User or Team-owned (also known as User-owned), or Organization-owned. Once the entity is created, this ownership setting cannot be changed. This is a design limitation due to how security and access control are enforced in CDS/Dataverse. Changing the ownership model would require structural changes to the underlying data and security roles.

This statement is correct. Once you create a user-owned custom entity in Dataverse, you cannot change the entity ownership from user to organization-owned. User-owned entities are specific to the user who created them and cannot be modified to be organization-owned.

explanation: The correct answer is False. Once an entity is created as user-owned, its ownership type cannot be changed to organization-owned. The ownership type is determined at the time of entity creation and remains fixed. If you need an organization-owned version, you would need to create a new entity with the correct ownership type and migrate data accordingly. Dataverse is an important topic in PL900 exam and below are important things to know about Dataverse. What Dataverse Is: Dataverse is a cloud-based data platform that allows you to securely store and manage data used by business applications. It provides a standardized and scalable data structure. Standard vs. Custom Tables: Standard tables (e.g., Contact, Account) come built-in. Custom tables can be created to match your specific business needs. Table Ownership Types. Use-Owned: Used when access control is based on who owns the data. Organization-Owned: Used for global data not tied to any individual user. Relationships Between TablesDataverse supports 1:N, N:1, and N:N relationships between tables to model business logic and data relationships. Business RulesBusiness Rules allow you to enforce logic and validation without writing code, right inside Dataverse. Security ModelDataverse uses a role-based security model with: Security Roles, Field-level security, Record-level security. Dataverse and Power Apps: Power Apps integrates tightly with Dataverse, letting you easily build model-driven and canvas apps that interact with data. Dataverse and Power Automate: You can create flows in Power Automate that trigger from Dataverse data changes, such as when a record is created, updated, or deleted. Dataverse Connectors and Integration: Dataverse can integrate with other systems through: Standard connectors, Custom connectors, Azure integration. Dataverse for Teams: A lite version of Dataverse included with Microsoft Teams. It allows you to build apps and flows directly in Teams without requiring a full Power Platform license. References: Update a record Owner and Owning Business Unit - Power Platform | Microsoft Learn Change entity/table scope to user from organization

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company wants to automatically generate a Dataverse table's structure just by describing the business requirements in plain language. Which capability supports this?

options.explanation: AI-assisted Dataverse table creation utilizes artificial intelligence to interpret and convert natural language descriptions of business requirements into the structure of a Dataverse table. This capability automates the process of creating tables based on the provided information, making it the suitable choice for the scenario described in the question.

The Desktop Flow Recorder is a tool used for recording and automating desktop tasks. It is not directly related to generating the structure of a Dataverse table based on natural language descriptions of business requirements, so it is not the correct choice for the scenario.

Solution Checker is a tool used to analyze and validate solutions built on the Power Platform for best practices and potential issues. It is not focused on automatically generating the structure of Dataverse tables based on natural language descriptions, so it is not the correct choice for the scenario described in the question.

explanation: Correct answer: Microsoft Dataverse supports AI-assisted creation of tables, columns, and relationships from natural language descriptions. Here is why this capability fits your scenario: How it works: When creating a new table, you select the start with Copilot option. You then simply type your business requirements in natural language (e.g., "Create a table for tracking real estate properties"). Automatic Generation: The artificial intelligence (AI) interprets your description to suggest table names, columns, data types, and relationships automatically. You can review, adjust, and generate the physical Microsoft Dataverse structure instantly. Other Options: Desktop Flow Recorder is a Power Automate tool that records mouse clicks and keystrokes to automate legacy apps. Solution Checker is used to evaluate custom solutions for performance and security compliance before exporting.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company keeps separate Development, Test, and Production environments. Why is this approach recommended?

options.text: A. To support application lifecycle management (ALM)
options.explanation: Having separate Development, Test, and Production environments allows for better application lifecycle management (ALM) practices. It enables developers to work on new features and fixes in the Development environment, test them in the Test environment, and then deploy them to the Production environment, ensuring a controlled and organized process.

options.text: B. To reduce Dataverse storage requirements
options.explanation: The separation of environments does not directly impact Dataverse storage requirements. While having separate environments may help in managing data and resources more effectively, it is not the primary reason for this approach.

The approach of having separate Development, Test, and Production environments is not related to eliminating security roles. Security roles are typically managed within each environment to control access and permissions for users.

The separation of environments does not directly impact internet speed. Internet speed is determined by external factors and is not influenced by the structure of Development, Test, and Production environments.

Power Automate Flows are not directly related to the reason why having separate Development, Test, and Production environments is recommended. The approach is more about managing the software development lifecycle and ensuring proper testing and deployment processes.

explanation: The correct answer is A. To support application lifecycle management (ALM). Separate environments are highly recommended for formal development processes. Here is why: Controlled Updates: You build and test new features without breaking the live app. Safe Testing: Devs can make mistakes in the Development environment without hurting real business data in Production. Staged Approvals: You securely move software step-by-step from Dev - Test - Production. Using separate environments helps organizations test changes before deploying them to production and supports a structured ALM process. The remaining options are unrelated. Resources

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A retail company's Power Apps app manages customer orders. After a new update, users report some features are broken, so the app maker restores an earlier version from the Version tab. What happens when that previous version is restored?

options.text: a) The current app is deleted permanently and cannot be recovered
options.explanation: Restoring a previous version of the app does not permanently delete the current app. It simply reverts the app to the selected earlier published version while keeping all versions in the history for reference or future restoration if needed.

options.text: b) The app is reverted to the selected earlier published version, but all versions remain in history
options.explanation: When the previous version is restored, the app is reverted to the selected earlier published version, but all versions remain in the history. This allows the app maker to access and restore any other version if necessary.

options.text: c) Only the restored version remains and all other versions are removed
options.explanation: Restoring a previous version does not remove all other versions from the history. All versions are retained for reference and potential restoration in the future, ensuring that the app maker has access to the full version history.

options.text: d) The app data in Dataverse is deleted and reset to default
options.explanation: Restoring a previous version of the app does not impact the app data in Dataverse. It only reverts the app to the selected earlier published version, maintaining the app data intact.

explanation: Power Apps keeps a version history of the app whenever it is published Each time you publish changes, a new version is created automatically You can restore any previous published version from the Version tab Restoring a version does not delete or remove other versions The restored version becomes the current active version of the app Only published versions are shown in version history Restoring a version does not affect Dataverse data Versioning is used to fix issues by rolling back to a working version Version history helps in tracking changes and troubleshooting problems Users always access the latest published (active) version of the app

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: Which FOUR capabilities does Microsoft Copilot Studio actually provide?

options.text: A. Publish agents to multiple channels
options.explanation: A. Publish agents to multiple channels is a capability available in Microsoft Copilot Studio, allowing users to distribute their agents across various communication channels for increased reach and accessibility.

options.text: B. Connect agents to Knowledge Sources
options.explanation: B. Connect agents to Knowledge Sources is a capability in Microsoft Copilot Studio that enables users to link their agents to knowledge sources, enhancing the accuracy and relevance of the information provided by the agents. Knowledge sources provide the information that the agent uses to answer questions. They can include: Websites SharePoint documents Dataverse data Uploaded files Example: If an employee asks, "What is our leave policy?", the agent searches its knowledge sources and provides an answer.

options.text: C. Use Tools to perform business actions
options.explanation: C. Use Tools to perform business actions is a capability in Microsoft Copilot Studio that provides users with tools to execute various business actions efficiently, streamlining processes and improving productivity. Tools allow the agent to perform actions and interact with external systems. Examples: Create a support ticket Look up customer information Send an email Trigger a Power Automate flow Think of tools as giving the agent the ability to do something, not just answer questions.

Topics is a capability available in Microsoft Copilot Studio, allowing users to categorize and organize information within the platform, making it easier to manage and access relevant data. Topics define the conversation flow and guide how the agent responds to specific user requests. Examples: Password reset process Vacation request process IT support troubleshooting Topics contain triggers, questions, conditions, and actions that determine how the conversation proceeds.
Creating SQL Server databases is not a capability available in Microsoft Copilot Studio. This choice is incorrect as it does not align with the functionalities of the platform.

options.text: F. Monitor agent usage and adoption
options.explanation: F. Monitor agent usage and adoption is not a capability available in Microsoft Copilot Studio. This choice is incorrect as it does not correspond to the features and capabilities of the platform.

explanation: Easy way to remember for PL-900 Knowledge Sources - Gives the agent information to answer questions. Tools - Lets the agent perform actions and connect to external systems. Topics - Controls conversation flows and guides user interactions. Views - Displays filtered data in Dataverse tables. Dashboards - Visualizes data and KPIs. Memory Trick KTT = Knowledge, Tools, Topics These are the three main building blocks of a Copilot Studio agent: Know - Knowledge Sources Take action - Tools Talk - Topics Views and Dashboards are for displaying and visualizing data, not for building or configuring agents. Resources

text: Solaris Tech is building a new app for Legal to manage contract approvals. The IT team asks: which tool is used to design a Power Pages site?

Power Apps Studio is a tool provided by Microsoft Power Platform for creating custom business applications without the need for extensive coding. While it is related to Power Pages, it is not the specific tool used for designing Power Pages. Power Apps Studio = Canvas & Model driven app builder Power Pages Design Studio = Website builder for Power Pages

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: At Evergreen Foods, building an app for Procurement to track supplier invoices, your manager Mr. Daniels stresses integration and asks: true or false, custom connectors can be reused across multiple platforms, including Power Apps, Power Automate, and Azure Logic Apps.

options.explanation: Q​: Is it true that custom connectors can be used across multiple platforms? A​: Yes, custom connectors are compatible with Power Apps, Power Automate, and Azure Logic Apps, making them highly versatile. Q​: What is a custom connector? A​: A custom connector is a reusable integration component that allows apps and workflows to communicate with APIs not natively supported by Microsoft platforms. Q​: What are the benefits of using custom connectors? A​: They offer increased flexibility, reduced development time, and improved security when integrating with external or proprietary APIs. Q​: Can custom connectors connect to private APIs? A​: Absolutely. They can be configured to connect to both public and private APIs, giving developers control over their data sources. Q​: What tools can be used to build custom connectors? A​: You can use Visual Studio Code, Power Platform CLI, and other development environments to create and manage custom connectors. Q​: How are custom connectors secured? A​: They support authentication protocols like OAuth 2.0, ensuring secure access to data and services. Q​: When should I consider building a custom connector? A​: If your data source isn’t natively supported by Power Apps, Power Automate, or Azure Logic Apps, a custom connector is an ideal solution. Q​: Do custom connectors help speed up development? A​: Yes, by abstracting API logic into reusable components, they streamline integration and reduce the time needed to build and maintain apps.

This statement is incorrect. Building custom connectors in Microsoft Power Platform provides the advantage of cross-platform usability, allowing them to be utilized in Power Apps, Power Automate, and Azure Logic Apps. This enhances the overall efficiency and flexibility of the integration and automation solutions developed within the Power Platform ecosystem.

explanation: The correct answer is - True. An advantage of building custom connectors is that they can be used in different platforms, such as Power Apps, Power Automate, and Azure Logic Apps. Here are some other advantages of building custom connectors: Increased flexibility: Custom connectors can be created to connect to any API, regardless of whether it is a public or private API. This gives users a lot of flexibility in terms of the data sources that they can connect to. Reduced development time: Custom connectors can be created using a variety of tools and technologies, including Visual Studio Code and Power Platform CLI. This can help to reduce the development time required to create a custom connector. Improved security: Custom connectors can be secured using OAuth 2.0 and other authentication protocols. This helps to protect the data that is being accessed through the custom connector. If you are looking for a way to connect to a data source that is not natively supported by Power Apps, Power Automate, or Azure Logic Apps, then building a custom connector is a great option. Exam Tips: The fundamentals are the focus of PL900. So simply understanding the features, functionalities, and how it operates should suffice. While delving into intricate details is beneficial, the exam places a premium on understanding fundamental concepts and processes.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Gemma built a canvas app using data stored in Excel and shared it with other Microsoft 365 users in her tenant, but they're getting a permissions error trying to load it. What should Gemma check?

options.text: That the users have a Power App per app / user license
options.explanation: Having a Power App per app / user license is not directly related to the permissions error when loading the Canvas app. This license is more about the user's ability to create and run Power Apps, rather than accessing shared apps.

options.text: That the users have the environment maker security role.
options.explanation: The environment maker security role is related to managing environments and settings within Power Platform, not directly linked to sharing data sources or resolving permissions errors when loading Canvas apps.

options.text: That she has also shared the data source (Excel file) with the users
options.explanation: The permissions error could be occurring because Gemma has not shared the data source (Excel file) with the users who are trying to access the Canvas app. Sharing the data source along with the app is essential for users to interact with the data. Q​: Do users need access to the Excel file used in a Power Apps canvas app? A​: Yes, users must have permission to access both the app and the underlying Excel file to ensure proper functionality. Q​: Where should the Excel file be stored for use in a canvas app? A​: It should be stored in a cloud location like OneDrive or SharePoint to enable secure and manageable sharing. Q​: What happens if users don’t have access to the Excel file? A​: The app may fail to load or display permission errors, even if the app itself has been shared correctly. Q​: How can Gemma ensure users have the right permissions? A​: She should share the Excel file with users via OneDrive or SharePoint, granting view or edit access based on how the app interacts with the data. Q​: Is sharing the app alone enough for users to interact with the data? A​: No, sharing the app does not automatically grant access to the data source. Both must be shared independently. Q​: What are the consequences of missing data source permissions? A​: Users may experience: App loading failures Permission errors Inability to view or modify data Q​: Can this issue be avoided with other data sources? A​: Yes, using Dataverse or SharePoint Lists can simplify permission management and reduce the risk of access issues.

options.text: That she has added the users as co-owners
options.explanation: Adding users as co-owners of the app may not directly resolve the permissions error related to accessing the data stored in Excel. While co-ownership of the app is important for collaboration and management, ensuring that the data source (Excel file) is shared with the users is crucial for resolving the permissions issue.

explanation: When you build a Power Apps canvas app using Excel as a data source, users need permission not only to access the app, but also to access the underlying Excel file. If the Excel file is stored in OneDrive or SharePoint, Gemma must ensure that the users have appropriate sharing permissions to view or edit the file depending on how the app interacts with it. Without access to the data source, the app will fail to load or throw permission errors, even if the app itself is shared correctly. Consequences of Missing Permissions: Without access to the Excel file, users may encounter: App loading failures Permission errors

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: At IronClad Security, you're building an app for Compliance to monitor audit findings. Working under project lead Victor, you need to answer: in what kind of scenario is it necessary to use a solution within Power Platform?

options.text: When creating security roles for apps and flows
options.explanation: Creating security roles for apps and flows can be done without the need for a solution in the Power Platform. Security roles can be managed directly within the environment settings.

options.text: When moving a collection of apps, flows, tables and more between environments
options.explanation: Using a solution is essential when moving a collection of apps, flows, tables, and more between environments in the Power Platform. Solutions help package and transfer components seamlessly across different environments. Q​: What is a Solution in the Power Platform? A​: A Solution is a container that bundles related components such as apps, flows, tables, and security roles—into a single package for deployment and management. Solution concepts with Power Platform - Power Platform | Microsoft Learn Q​: Why are Solutions important in Power Platform development? A​: They allow you to organize, transport, and version your customizations across environments like development, testing, and production. Q​: What components can be included in a Solution? A​: Solutions can include canvas apps, model-driven apps, flows, tables, forms, views, dashboards, security roles, and more. Q​: What’s the difference between managed and unmanaged Solutions? A​: Unmanaged Solutions are editable and used during development. Managed Solutions are locked and used in production to ensure stability and controlled updates. Q​: Can Solutions be versioned and updated? A​: Yes, Solutions support versioning, allowing you to track changes and apply updates systematically, especially in managed environments. Q​: How do Solutions help with environment migration? A​: They package all necessary components so you can export from one environment and import into another, preserving relationships and configurations. Q​: Are Solutions only for developers? A​: No, both developers and power users can use Solutions to organize and deploy their work efficiently within the Power Platform. Q​: Can I use Solutions to share apps with others? A​: Yes, Solutions are a reliable way to distribute apps and related components across teams or organizations.

options.text: To store all the data from Dataverse correctly

options.text: To apply updates to the apps

explanation: Solutions: Solutions are containers in the Power Platform that bundle related components like apps, flows, tables, security roles, and more into a single package. Why others are wrong: Creating security roles: You can do this outside a solution, though roles can be added to a solution if part of a deployment. text: During a training workshop at NovaTech, the facilitator asks: true or false, Power Apps is a no-code/low-code platform that lets you build applications using your existing business knowledge and skills.

Users can leverage their existing skills and business knowledge to build apps efficiently. Q​: What is Power Apps? A​: Power Apps is a No-code/Low-code platform that enables users to build custom business applications using their domain expertise and existing skills without needing deep programming knowledge. Q​: What types of apps can I build with Power Apps? A​: Power Apps offers Canvas apps for pixel-perfect design, Model-driven apps for data-centric solutions, and Portals (now Power Pages) for external-facing websites. Q​: Can Power Apps apps run on mobile devices? Q​: Do I need to change my business processes to fit Power Apps? A​: Not at all. Q​: Is Power Apps suitable for non-developers? A​: Absolutely. Its intuitive drag-and-drop interface and integration with Microsoft tools make it accessible to business users, analysts, and citizen developers. This statement is incorrect. Power Apps is specifically designed as a no-code/low-code platform, allowing users to create applications without the need for advanced coding skills. It emphasizes ease of use and accessibility for users with varying levels of technical expertise.

explanation: The correct answer is True. Snippets of Power Apps: 1. Power Apps is a No-code/Low-code platform that allows you to build apps with your business knowledge and existing skills. 2.
