options.explanation: Data is a crucial component of model-driven apps in Microsoft Power Platform as it defines the structure and relationships of the data used within the application. It includes entities, fields, relationships, and data types that drive the functionality of the app.

User Interface (UI) is an essential component of model-driven apps as it determines how users interact with the application. It includes forms, views, dashboards, and navigation elements that provide a user-friendly experience.

Logic plays a vital role in model-driven apps as it defines the business rules, workflows, and processes that govern the behavior of the application. It includes business rules, workflows, plugins, and custom code that automate tasks and enforce business logic.

Visualization components are important in model-driven apps as they allow users to visualize and analyze data within the application. This includes charts, graphs, dashboards, and reports that help users make informed decisions based on the data presented.

explanation: A well-designed model-driven app consists of several components that are used to build the appearance and functionality of the finished app. The components and component properties that makers use to create an app become what is known as the app's metadata. To build off the concepts in the previous unit, and to better understand how each of these components relates to app design, we can categorize them into four categories: Data User interface (UI) Logic Visualization components4 Components of model-driven-apps - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Which of these are actual types of views supported in model-driven apps? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Personal views are views that are created and customized by individual users to suit their specific needs and preferences within the model-driven app. These views are private to the user who creates them and can be used to filter, sort, and display data in a way that is most useful to them.

System views are predefined views that are created by system administrators or developers and are available to all users of the model-driven app. These views are typically used to provide a consistent way of viewing and interacting with data across the organization.

Public views are views that are created by system administrators or developers and are shared with specific groups or roles within the organization. These views are accessible to multiple users and can be used to provide a standardized way of viewing and analyzing data.

Workflow views are not supported in model-driven apps. Workflow views are specific to automated processes and are used to track the progress and status of workflows within the app. They are not used for displaying data in the same way as personal, system, or public views.

Dashboard views are not types of views supported in model-driven apps. Dashboards are separate components that provide a visual representation of key data and metrics from multiple sources within the app. They are used for high-level data analysis and monitoring, but they are not considered views in the traditional sense within the app.

explanation: Before we explore how to create views, it's important to understand the different types of views that are available. Model-driven apps support three types of views, each serving distinct purposes: Personal views: Custom views created and owned by individual users within the system. Personal views are only visible to the user who created them unless explicitly shared with others. Users have full control over these views and can customize them to meet their specific needs. This includes filtering data, organizing information, or displaying specific fields. System views: These predefined views are part of the core functionality of the system. Examples of system views include Quick Find, which is used for rapid searches; Advanced Find, which enables complex queries (also used to create personal views); Associated Views, which display related records; and Lookup Views, used for selecting records in lookup fields. Unlike personal views, system views are managed at the administrative level, meaning only system administrators or customizers have the authority to modify them. Their design ensures consistency and reliability across the application, supporting essential operations and interactions. Public views: Public views are views that are accessible to all users within the application. These views can be customized to meet the specific needs of an organization. They're often used in subgrids, which display related records within forms, or dashboards, where they provide a summarized view of key data points. Create and modify views - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: What's the main advantage of combining desktop flows with cloud flows in Power Automate?

options.text: B. They enable comprehensive automation by bridging local machine tasks with cloudbased services
options.explanation: The main advantage of combining desktop flows and cloud flows in Power Automate is that it enables comprehensive automation by bridging local machine tasks with cloud-based services. This integration allows for a seamless workflow between tasks that need to be performed on a local machine and those that require cloud-based services, enhancing the overall automation capabilities.

options.text: C. They replace the need for Dataverse security roles and permissions
options.explanation: Combining desktop flows and cloud flows in Power Automate does not replace the need for Dataverse security roles and permissions. Dataverse security roles and permissions are specific to managing access and security within the Dataverse environment and are not directly related to the integration of desktop and cloud flows.

options.text: D. They are only useful for automating manual button clicks in canvas apps
options.explanation: Desktop flows and cloud flows in Power Automate are not limited to automating manual button clicks in canvas apps only. While they can be used for this purpose, their main advantage lies in enabling comprehensive automation by bridging local machine tasks with cloud-based services, providing a wider range of automation possibilities beyond just button clicks in canvas apps.

explanation: Desktop flows and cloud flows serve distinct purposes, but together they offer a powerful way to automate tasks across different environments. Desktop flows are tailored for automating processes on your local machine, such as interacting with installed software, legacy applications, or performing repetitive tasks like data entry. On the other hand, cloud flows are designed to connect and automate tasks across cloud-based services and platforms, enabling seamless integration between tools like Outlook, SharePoint, Teams, and more. Describe use cases for cloud and desktop flows - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: True or false: every app user must be assigned at least one predefined or custom security role.
explanation: Model-driven apps utilize role-based security to manage sharing and access control. This means that each security role includes a set of privileges, which define the specific actions users can perform on tables within the app. This means that structure allows for differentiated access levels: for example, two users may both use an app, but one user might only have permission to read records or view records they personally created, whereas another user could have broader access, such as viewing all records and even deleting them. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A field technician using a canvas app built in Power Apps needs to quickly check a service request's status while on site, without digging through multiple screens. Instead, they simply type "What is the status of the current service request?" and get a real-time answer straight from the app's connected data source. Which Power Apps capability does this demonstrate?

options.explanation: Power Automate workflows are used to automate repetitive tasks and integrate different applications and services. While they can be used to trigger actions based on specific events, they are not directly related to providing real-time updates within a canvas app in response to user input.

options.text: B. Copilot controls in Power Apps
options.explanation: Copilot controls in Power Apps are designed to provide intelligent suggestions and guidance to users as they build apps. In this scenario, Copilot controls can interpret the user's input and fetch real-time data from the connected data source to quickly provide the status of the current service request without the need for manual navigation.

options.text: C. System views in modeldriven apps
options.explanation: System views in model-driven apps are used to display filtered lists of records based on predefined criteria. While they can help organize and present data within the app, they do not offer the real-time interaction and immediate updates that are required in this situation.

explanation: Copilot controls in Power Apps bring AI-powered capabilities directly into canvas apps, enabling users to interact with app data through natural language inputs. These controls are designed to enhance productivity by simplifying data exploration and automating responses to user queries. In this learning unit, you explore how Copilot controls work, their practical applications, and how they can be customized to fit your app’s needs. What are Copilot controls? Think of Copilot controls act as intelligent assistants embedded within your app. They allow users to ask questions or perform actions using conversational language, making it easier to access insights and interact with data without needing complex navigation or manual input. Boost productivity: Copilot controls streamline workflows by providing AI-generated answers to questions about app data. For example, a user might ask, "What are the top-selling products this month?" and receive an immediate response based on the app’s connected data source. Optimize for mobile users: These controls are valuable for mobile users who need quick access to information. Instead of navigating through multiple screens, users can type or speak their query and get instant results. Example: A field technician using a mobile app could ask, "What is the status of the current service request?" and receive real-time updates without searching manually. Describe the capabilities of Copilot controls - Training | Microsoft Learn

The correct sequence requires navigating to Settings in Power Apps Studio (B) before enabling Copilot features and saving the app (A).

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which of these are genuinely valid use cases for desktop flows in Power Automate? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Organizing files automatically, such as sorting invoices into the correct folders
options.explanation: Desktop flows in Power Automate can be used to automate the process of organizing files automatically, such as sorting invoices into the correct folders. This helps in streamlining file management tasks and improving efficiency.

options.text: B. Extracting data from websites and storing it in Excel for analysis
options.explanation: Desktop flows can extract data from websites and store it in Excel for analysis. This automation saves time and reduces manual effort required to gather and organize data from various sources.

options.text: C. Interacting with legacy applications by simulating clicks, typing, and navigation
options.explanation: Desktop flows are useful for interacting with legacy applications by simulating clicks, typing, and navigation. This allows users to automate tasks that involve working with older systems that may not have APIs or integrations.

options.text: D. Automating repetitive office tasks like updating statuses or generating reports
options.explanation: Automating repetitive office tasks like updating statuses or generating reports is a valid use case for desktop flows in Power Automate. This helps in improving productivity by automating routine tasks and freeing up time for more strategic activities.

options.text: E. Receiving daily information updates, such as weather or stock prices, without manual effort
options.explanation: Desktop flows can be used to receive daily information updates, such as weather or stock prices, without manual effort. This automation ensures that users stay informed without having to manually check for updates regularly.

options.text: F. Organizing client invoices and receipts efficiently for freelancers or small businesses
options.explanation: Organizing client invoices and receipts efficiently for freelancers or small businesses can be achieved using desktop flows in Power Automate. This automation helps in managing financial documents effectively and reducing the time spent on manual organization tasks.

explanation: Here are some examples of desktop flow use cases: Organizing files automatically: Imagine you frequently download reports or images from emails and need to sort them into specific folders. With desktop flows, you can set up an automated process to move files into designated folders based on their names or file types. For instance, all PDF invoices could automatically be sorted into a folder named "Invoices," saving you time and effort. Extracting data from websites: Suppose you're tracking product prices or gathering information from a weather website. Desktop flows can automate web scraping tasks, pulling data from websites and storing it neatly in an Excel spreadsheet. This capability eliminates the need for manual copying and pasting, allowing you to focus on analyzing the data instead. Interacting with legacy applications: Many businesses still rely on older systems like terminal emulators or applications that require manual input via user interfaces. Desktop flows can simulate human actions, such as clicking buttons, entering text, or navigating menus, using UI elements, images, or even screen coordinates. For example, you could automate data entry into an outdated Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system that doesn't support modern APIs. Desktop flows are incredibly versatile and cater to a wide range of users. A weather enthusiast might want to automate the process of receiving daily updates from weather websites. An office employee reducing the time spent on repetitive data entry tasks in legacy systems. Or a freelancer organizing client invoices and receipts efficiently. By using desktop flows, you can simplify complex processes and reduce errors. Power Automate also has prebuilt templates you can use as a starting point and customize to meet your needs. References: Describe use cases for cloud and desktop flows - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Your company still runs a legacy ERP system installed on local machines with no modern API support, but you need to pull data out of it and share the results with your team in SharePoint. Which Power Automate approach would best achieve this end-to-end?

options.text: A. Use cloud flow to connect Outlook and SharePoint

options.text: B. Use desktop flow to simulate clicks and extract data
options.explanation: Using a desktop flow to simulate clicks and extract data may not be the most efficient approach for extracting data from a legacy ERP system. While desktop flows can automate tasks on local machines, they may not provide a seamless solution for extracting data from the ERP system and sharing it with the team in SharePoint.

options.text: C. Combine a desktop flow to extract data locally with a cloud flow to upload it to SharePoint
options.explanation: Combining a desktop flow to extract data locally with a cloud flow to upload it to SharePoint would be the best approach for achieving end-to-end automation in this scenario. The desktop flow can extract data from the legacy ERP system installed on local machines, while the cloud flow can seamlessly upload the extracted data to SharePoint for sharing with the team.

options.text: This is not possible in Power Automate
options.explanation: It is possible to achieve end-to-end automation in Power Automate by combining different types of flows to extract data from a legacy ERP system and share it with the team in SharePoint. Therefore, this scenario is feasible in Power Automate.

explanation: Combine a desktop flow to extract data locally with a cloud flow to upload it to SharePoint By combining desktop and cloud flows, you can create comprehensive, end-to-end automation solutions that bridge the gap between your local environment and the cloud. For example, you could use a desktop flow to extract data from a legacy application on your computer and then use a cloud flow to upload that data to a SharePoint folder or send it via email. This integration allows you to streamline workflows across both physical and virtual systems, maximizing efficiency and reducing manual effort. Describe use cases for cloud and desktop flows - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You want a flow that sends a quick reminder email whenever a user clicks a button in Power Apps. Which option should you choose?

options.text: A. Start the flow when a user manually initiates it.
options.explanation: Starting the flow when a user manually initiates it by clicking a button in Power Apps is the correct choice for this scenario. This ensures that the reminder email is sent only when the user triggers the flow, providing a quick and personalized reminder based on user interaction.

options.text: B. Start the flow when a new email is received from a specific sender
options.explanation: Starting the flow when a new email is received from a specific sender is not relevant to the requirement of sending a quick reminder email when a user clicks a button in Power Apps. This choice does not align with the desired functionality and would not achieve the intended outcome.

options.text: C. Run the flow automatically every Monday morning at 9 AM
options.explanation: Running the flow automatically every Monday morning at 9 AM is not suitable for sending a quick reminder email when a user clicks a button in Power Apps. This choice is based on a scheduled time rather than user interaction, which does not meet the specific requirement outlined in the question.

options.text: D. Start the flow when a new file is added to OneDrive
options.explanation: Starting the flow when a new file is added to OneDrive is not the appropriate option for sending a quick reminder email when a user clicks a button in Power Apps. This choice is focused on file-related triggers and does not address the user-initiated action required for sending the reminder email.

explanation: Instant Triggers: These triggers are manually activated by the user. For instance, you might use an instant trigger to send a quick reminder email with just a button click. Creating an instant flow: An instant flow is designed to execute tasks immediately upon a manual trigger, making it ideal for scenarios where users need on-demand automation. For example, you could associate an instant flow with a device such as a flick button. When the button is pushed, it launches the flow. To create an instant flow, start by selecting the "Instant cloud flow" option in Power Automate. You need to select how to trigger the flow: "Manually trigger a flow," or "When Power Apps calls a flow," which allows users to initiate the process with a button click. For example, you could create an instant flow that sends a prewritten email to a team when a project milestone is achieved. Once the trigger is set, define the subsequent actions, such as sending notifications, updating records, or generating reports. This type of flow is perfect for tasks requiring user intervention to start the process. Create a cloud flow by using an instant, automated, or scheduled trigger - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You want to automatically generate and email a weekly sales-performance report every Monday morning with no manual work. Which option should you choose?

options.explanation: Instant flow is triggered manually by a user or an event, and it does not support scheduling the flow to run automatically at a specific time. Therefore, it is not suitable for generating and emailing a weekly sales performance report every Monday morning without manual intervention.

Scheduled Flow allows you to schedule the flow to run automatically at specific times, making it the correct choice for generating and emailing a weekly sales performance report every Monday morning without manual intervention. This option ensures the report is sent out consistently without the need for manual triggering.

Automated flow is a generic term and does not specifically refer to a flow type that supports scheduling for automatic execution at specific times. Without the ability to schedule the flow, it would not be suitable for generating and emailing a weekly sales performance report every Monday morning without manual intervention.

Business flow is not a recognized term in the context of Microsoft Power Platform flows. Without a clear definition or functionality associated with this option, it is not a valid choice for generating and emailing a weekly sales performance report every Monday morning without manual intervention.

explanation: Creating a Scheduled Flow: Scheduled flows run at predefined intervals, making them perfect for recurring tasks like data backups or report generation. To create a scheduled flow, Select the "Scheduled cloud flow" option and specify the frequency and timing for the flow to run, such as daily, weekly, or monthly. For example, you could set up a scheduled flow to generate and email a sales performance report every Monday morning. Once the schedule is configured, add the necessary actions, such as querying data, compiling reports, or sending reminders. Scheduled flows ensure consistency and reliability for time-sensitive tasks without requiring manual oversight. Create a cloud flow by using an instant, automated, or scheduled trigger - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment

explanation: What Is the Power Platform Admin Center? text: A hospital wants to build an app for managing patient records. It needs to securely store structured data, support relationships between patients and doctors, and integrate easily with other Power Platform tools. Which solution should they use?

options.text: a) Excel files stored in OneDrive
options.explanation: Storing patient records in Excel files on OneDrive may not provide the necessary security and structure required for managing sensitive healthcare data. It may also lack the ability to support relationships between patients and doctors efficiently.

Dataverse tables are the correct solution for securely storing structured data, supporting relationships between patients and doctors, and integrating easily with other Power Platform tools. Dataverse provides a secure and scalable database for managing healthcare data effectively.

Power BI datasets are primarily used for data visualization and analytics, not for storing and managing structured patient records. While Power BI can be integrated with other Power Platform tools, it may not be the most suitable solution for managing patient records.

SharePoint pages are more suitable for document management and collaboration, rather than securely storing structured patient records and supporting relationships between patients and doctors. SharePoint may not provide the necessary data structure and integration capabilities required for a healthcare app.

explanation: The hospital needs a solution that can: Securely store patient information Manage structured healthcare data Support relationships between patients and doctors Integrate with Power Platform tools Microsoft Dataverse is the best choice because it is designed to handle relational business data securely and efficiently. Why Dataverse Tables Are the Best Solution Secure Data Storage Dataverse provides: Role-based security Row-level security Encryption and access control This is important because hospital and patient data is highly sensitive. Structured Data Management Dataverse stores data in tables similar to a relational database. Example tables: Patients Doctors Appointments Medical Records This makes healthcare information organized and easy to manage. Supports Relationships Dataverse allows relationships between tables. Example: One doctor - many patients One patient - many appointments This helps the hospital connect related healthcare records efficiently.

text: A business user wants to quickly build a flow just by describing the process in natural language, rather than manually configuring each step. Which capability would let them do this?

What Copilot Can Automatically Do Create flow steps Suggest triggers Add actions Configure connectors Build approval workflows Recommend automation logic

Dataverse tables are used to store and manage data within the Power Platform environment. While they are essential for data storage and organization, they are not directly related to the ability to build flows by describing the process in natural language.

explanation: A business user wants to create a flow quickly without manually adding every trigger, action, and condition. In this situation, Copilot in Power Automate is the best solution because it allows users to describe the automation process using natural language. The AI-powered Copilot understands the description and automatically generates the flow structure. The user simply types a request such as: “When a new file is added to SharePoint, send an approval email to the manager and notify the team in Teams.” Copilot then: Interprets the request Identifies the trigger Adds the required actions Creates the flow automatically This reduces the need for manual configuration.

text: A company builds a Power Pages site for external users and wants to control what each user can see at the record level in Dataverse. What should they configure?

options.text: c) Table permissions with web roles

explanation:
When users access data through a Power Pages website, the company must control: Who can log in. What data they can access. Which records they can view/edit/delete.

This is done using: Web Roles. Table Permissions.

Together, they provide record-level security for Dataverse data. In Microsoft Power Pages, a web role is similar to a user role/security group. It defines: WHAT TYPE OF USER someone is.

Examples: Customer, Employee, Manager, Partner, Admin.

Think of web roles like: “Job titles” for portal users. Table permissions define: WHAT DATA users can access inside Dataverse.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: In a Power Platform canvas app, which component is mainly responsible for enabling user input, things like text boxes, dropdown lists, and sliders on the screen?

options.explanation: Form Processor is not primarily responsible for enabling user input through elements like text boxes, dropdowns, and sliders on a canvas app screen in Power Platform. It is more related to processing and analyzing form data rather than enabling user input.

Form Factor is not primarily responsible for enabling user input through elements like text boxes, dropdowns, and sliders on a canvas app screen in Power Platform. Form Factor typically refers to the physical size and shape of a device or component, not user input elements.

Form Controls are primarily responsible for enabling user input through elements like text boxes, dropdowns, and sliders on a canvas app screen in Power Platform. These controls allow users to interact with the app and input data for processing.

None of these choices are correct as Form Controls are the primary components responsible for enabling user input through elements like text boxes, dropdowns, and sliders on a canvas app screen in Power Platform. Form Processor and Form Factor are not directly related to user input elements in this context.

explanation: The correct answer is Form controls. 1. Form controls are part of Power Apps, not Power BI.  Form controls refer to interactive elements or components that you can add to your canvas apps, model-driven apps, or Power pages to collect, display, or manipulate data. Eg Text Input: Allows users to enter text or numbers. Label: Displays text or instructions to users. Button: Triggers actions when clicked, such as submitting a form or navigating to another screen. Checkbox: Allows users to make binary choices (checked or unchecked). Radio Button: Presents a list of options, but users can select only one. 2. Form factor describes the size of the hardware that is used to open reports, and to page orientation (portrait or landscape). Layout Design: Form factor relates to how visuals and components are arranged and sized within a report or dashboard canvas. Responsive Design: It includes considerations for making visuals responsive to different screen sizes and orientations. Optimal Display: Ensures that visuals are displayed effectively on various devices, from desktop monitors to mobile screens. Consistency: A consistent form factor across visuals maintains a professional and organized appearance. Orientation: It also involves choosing between portrait (vertical) or landscape (horizontal) orientation for the report page, which affects how visuals fit on the page. User Experience: A well-considered form factor enhances the user experience by providing clear, easily navigable reports. Exam Tips: Doing well in the PL-900 exam means you should understand all the words, meanings, special terms, and how things look in the Power Platform apps. If you don't know these terms, it will be hard to pick the right answers.

text: Fill in the blank: after creating a canvas app, to let users share it with others, you need to grant them the ________________ permission.

options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Granting the User permission to users would not allow them to share the canvas app with others. This permission level typically only allows basic access and usage of the app, not sharing capabilities.

Granting the Co-Owner permission to users is the correct choice as it allows users to share the canvas app with others. Co-Owners have full control over the app, including the ability to share it with additional users.

This option is incorrect. Granting the Environment Maker permission to users would not necessarily allow them to share the canvas app with others. This permission level is more focused on managing and configuring the environment settings, rather than sharing individual canvas apps.

explanation: Power Apps Roles Overview: 1. Co-owner Can edit and share apps that have been shared with them. Can customize the app, update components, and modify logic. Helps in collaborative app development. Cannot delete or take ownership away from the original creator. 2. User Can only view and run the app. Cannot make changes or share it with others. Role is assigned when the app is shared in "play-only" mode. Ideal for end-users of the app in a business environment. 3. Environment Maker Can create resources (apps, flows, connections) in an environment. Does not automatically get access to all apps within the environment. Grants permissions at the environment level, not per app. Useful for developers or power users who build solutions across multiple apps. This is ideal for customer portals, partner access, or any scenario requiring public interaction with Dataverse data. 2. Canvas apps - Connect to multiple data sources. Canvas apps offer a highly customizable drag-and-drop interface to build apps that can connect to a wide variety of data sources not just Dataverse but also SharePoint, Excel, SQL, and many others giving flexibility in app design and data integration. 3. Model-driven apps - Use business process flows to guide the user. Model-driven apps are built on Dataverse with a focus on structured data and processes. They include built-in business process flows that guide users step-by-step through complex workflows, ensuring consistency and compliance.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Which security method requires users to verify their identity through a mobile app or biometric scan, to cut down the risk of unauthorized access?

options.explanation: Password complexity rules focus on setting requirements for the complexity of passwords, such as length, special characters, and numbers. While important for overall security, they do not directly involve verifying identity through a mobile app or biometric scan.

Multifactor authentication (MFA) is the correct choice as it requires users to verify their identity through multiple methods, such as a password, mobile app, or biometric scan. This additional layer of security helps reduce the risk of unauthorized access by ensuring that the person trying to access the system is who they claim to be.

Single sign-on (SSO) is a method that allows users to access multiple applications with a single set of login credentials. While it can improve user experience and streamline access, it does not specifically involve verifying identity through a mobile app or biometric scan to reduce unauthorized access.

Data encryption involves encoding data to protect it from unauthorized access. While encryption is crucial for securing sensitive information, it does not directly involve verifying user identity through a mobile app or biometric scan as a method to reduce the risk of unauthorized access.

explanation: To strengthen security, it supports multifactor authentication (MFA), requiring users to verify their identity through other steps, such as a mobile app or biometric scan. This reduces the risk of unauthorized access, even if passwords are compromised.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power Automate cloud flow that needs to reach data from a third-party application exposing a REST API, but no prebuilt connector exists for it. Which TWO approaches could you use? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Applying a data policy is not a valid approach to accessing data from a third-party application that exposes a REST API. Data policies are typically used for managing data governance, compliance, and security within an organization, and do not directly facilitate integration with external APIs.

options.text: Create a custom connector for the REST API
options.explanation: Creating a custom connector for the REST API is a valid approach to accessing data from a third-party application that does not have a prebuilt connector. Custom connectors allow you to define the endpoints, authentication methods, and actions specific to the API, enabling seamless integration with Power Automate flows.

options.text: Use the builtin HTTP action in Power Automate to call the REST API directly
options.explanation: Using the built-in HTTP action in Power Automate to call the REST API directly is another valid approach to accessing data from a third-party application. This action allows you to make HTTP requests to the API endpoints, retrieve data, and perform operations without the need for a custom connector.

explanation: For PL900 exam point of view, knowing the below is sufficient: Using the HTTP connector is a valid solution for accessing data in a third-party application with a REST API when there is no specific connector available is sufficient. Creating a custom connector is a valid solution for accessing data in a third-party application with a REST API when there is no pre-built connector available What is REST API? One system (called the client) sends a request to another system (called the server). The server processes the request and sends back a response, usually in a format like JSON. REST APIs use standard web methods like GET (to read data), POST (to create data), PUT (to update data), and DELETE (to remove data). These interactions happen over HTTP, the same protocol your browser uses to load websites. REST APIs are popular because they’re easy to use, scalable, and work well with many types of applications.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Contoso Ltd. wants to manage permissions efficiently across its Power Platform environment. What's the main purpose of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)?

options.text: A) To assign usernames and passwords to all users
options.explanation: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is not primarily focused on assigning usernames and passwords to users. Its main purpose is to define and manage user roles, permissions, and access levels within an organization's systems and applications.

options.text: B) To define what actions users can perform and what data they can access
options.explanation: This choice is correct because the primary purpose of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is to determine what actions users can take and what data they can access based on their roles and responsibilities within the organization. RBAC helps enforce security policies and restrict unauthorized access to sensitive information.

options.text: C) To encrypt all application data
options.explanation: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) does not primarily focus on encrypting application data. While encryption can be a security measure within RBAC, its main function is to control user access based on predefined roles and permissions.

options.text: D) To create backups of all user records
options.explanation: Creating backups of user records is not the primary purpose of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). RBAC is more about managing and controlling user access rights and permissions within an organization's systems and applications.

explanation: Role-based access control (RBAC) allows administrators to assign security roles to users that define what actions they can perform and what data they can access. For example, a "System Administrator" role might grant full control over all resources, while a "Basic User" role might allow viewing specific records but not making changes. RBAC operates at multiple levels: Environment-level access: Controls access to apps, flows, and resources within specific environments, such as development or production. App-level access: Restricts access to individual apps or components within an environment. Record-level access: Provides granular control over who can view, edit, or delete specific records. References: Describe the Power Platform security model - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: You're documenting guidelines for an ongoing project at Contoso Ltd., and need to answer: what's the primary goal of the principle of least privilege?

options.text: A) To grant users full access to all resources
options.explanation: Granting users full access to all resources goes against the principle of least privilege, which aims to restrict access to only the necessary resources to minimize the risk of unauthorized access and potential security breaches.

options.text: B) To ensure users only have the permissions they need
options.explanation: The primary goal of the principle of least privilege is to ensure that users only have the permissions they need to perform their specific tasks or roles. This helps reduce the attack surface and limits the potential damage that can be caused by compromised accounts.

options.text: C) To prevent users from accessing any resources
options.explanation: Preventing users from accessing any resources is not the goal of the principle of least privilege. Instead, it focuses on limiting access to only the essential resources required for users to fulfill their job responsibilities, enhancing security and reducing risks.

options.text: D) To allow administrators to bypass security protocols
options.explanation: Allowing administrators to bypass security protocols contradicts the principle of least privilege, which advocates for restricting access rights to the minimum necessary for users to carry out their tasks effectively and securely.

explanation: Users can have multiple security roles assigned to them. This allows organizations to easily provide access to resources, apps, and records as needed. By following the principle of least privilege access, users only have the permissions they need, reducing risks from accidental or malicious actions. Administrators can easily assign and update roles as organizational needs evolve, balancing accessibility with protection.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which of these correctly describe how Copilot can be used in Power Platform? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Copilot can generate flows in Power Automate using natural language prompts.
options.explanation: Copilot in Power Platform can indeed generate flows in Power Automate by interpreting natural language prompts, making it easier for users to create automated workflows without the need for extensive coding knowledge.

options.text: Copilot allows you to build desktop flows by narrating and demonstrating tasks with Record with Copilot.
options.explanation: Copilot offers the feature of building desktop flows through narration and task demonstration with Record with Copilot, enabling users to easily create automation sequences by showcasing the steps.

options.text: Copilot can automatically fix all configuration errors in a flow without user input.
options.explanation: Copilot does not have the capability to automatically fix all configuration errors in a flow without user input. Users still need to review and correct any errors detected by Copilot.

options.text: Copilot helps refine flows by inserting new actions (e.g., “Insert SMS notification after the last action”).
options.explanation: Copilot assists in refining flows by suggesting and inserting new actions based on user input, such as adding an SMS notification after a specific action, enhancing the efficiency of flow creation and customization.

options.text: Copilot can be used across Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI to assist with app building, automation, and insights.
options.explanation: Copilot is a versatile tool that can be utilized across Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI to support users in various tasks like app development, automation, and data insights, providing a unified experience within the Power Platform ecosystem.

options.text: Copilot requires advanced scripting knowledge to create flows.
options.explanation: Copilot is designed to simplify the process of creating flows and does not require advanced scripting knowledge. It aims to assist users with different levels of expertise in building automated workflows without the need for extensive coding skills.

explanation: Power Apps (App Building) Natural language app creation: You can describe what you want (e.g., “Build an app to track employee leave requests”), and Copilot generates the app structure. Data integration: Copilot helps connect to data sources like Dataverse, SharePoint, or Excel, automatically suggesting tables and relationships. UI suggestions: It can recommend layouts, forms, and controls based on your description, reducing manual design work. Formula assistance: Copilot suggests Power Fx formulas, helping nontechnical users implement logic without deep coding knowledge. Iterative refinement: You can adjust prompts (“Add a gallery to show pending requests”) and Copilot updates the app accordingly. Power Automate (Automation) Flow creation with prompts: Copilot builds flows from natural language instructions, e.g., “When a new file is added to SharePoint, send me an email.” Record with Copilot (AI Recorder): Narrate and demonstrate desktop tasks; Copilot captures mouse, keyboard, and voice to generate desktop flows. Action insertion: You can ask Copilot to add steps like “Insert SMS notification after the last action.” Error handling guidance: Copilot suggests fixes when Flow Checker identifies issues, making troubleshooting easier. Optimization support: It can recommend streamlining flows by removing redundant actions or adjusting triggers. Testing and refinement: Copilot helps validate flows and suggests improvements after test runs. Power Pages (Websites/Portals) Content generation: Copilot assists in drafting text for web pages, FAQs, or instructions, based on your prompts. Form creation: You can describe the type of form you need (e.g., “Create a registration form for new users”), and Copilot generates it. Styling suggestions: Copilot can recommend themes, layouts, and design adjustments to improve usability. Data integration: It helps connect Power Pages to Dataverse or other sources, ensuring forms and portals capture and display data correctly. Accessibility improvements: Copilot suggests adjustments to make pages more user-friendly and compliant with accessibility standards. Rapid prototyping: Ideal for quickly spinning up portals without needing deep web development skills. Key takeaway: In Power Apps, Copilot accelerates app design and logic building. In Power Automate, it simplifies flow creation and desktop automation. In Power Pages, it speeds up content, form, and portal development.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: In a Power Apps canvas app, which menu lets you add new components, text boxes, input fields, media controls, to the app screen?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect. The Home Menu in Canvas Apps typically contains options related to the overall layout and design of the app, such as themes, backgrounds, and app settings. It does not provide options for adding new components like text, input, or media controls.

The Insert Menu in Canvas Apps is where you can find options to add new components such as text, input, and media controls to your app. This menu is specifically designed for inserting new elements into the app canvas, making it the correct choice for adding new components.

This option is incorrect. The View Menu in Canvas Apps usually contains options related to the display and navigation of the app, such as zoom settings, gridlines, and rulers. It does not offer options for adding new components like text, input, or media controls.

This option is incorrect. The Action Menu in Canvas Apps typically contains options related to app functionality, such as adding actions, workflows, or automation. It does not provide options for adding new visual components like text, input, or media controls to the app canvas.

explanation: Exam Tips: Know each menu's purposeFocus on what each menu (Insert, Home, View, Action) is primarily used for, this is frequently tested. Associate tasks with menusMemorize what tasks go with what menus: adding controls (Insert), formatting (Home), etc.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Power Automate flows can be triggered in different ways. A flow started manually when a user presses a button in the app or on a mobile device is commonly called a button flow. What's another name for a button flow?

options.explanation: An instant flow, also known as a button flow, is triggered manually by a user clicking a button to initiate the flow. This type of flow is typically used for on-demand, immediate actions in response to user input.

This option is incorrect. An automated flow is a type of flow that is triggered automatically based on predefined conditions or events. It does not require manual intervention to start the flow, unlike a button flow.

This option is incorrect. A scheduled flow is a type of flow that is triggered at specific times or intervals according to a predefined schedule. It is not the same as a button flow, which is initiated manually by a user.

explanation: Exam Tips: Button flow is the informal name for an instant flow in Power Automate. Instant flows are triggered manually by the user - for example, tapping a button in the Power Automate mobile app or selecting a button in Power Apps. They are useful for tasks that need to be run on demand, such as sending quick notifications, creating records, or starting approvals. Other flow types include: Automated flows -> triggered by events (e.g., new email, record created). Scheduled flows Knowing the different types of flows is very important for PL900 exam.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Power Automate has a tool called Flow Checker available while you're building flows. What's its main function?

options.text: Allows you to go into past runs and check whether they worked.
options.explanation: Flow Checker in Power Automate is not designed to allow you to go into past runs and check whether they worked. Its primary function is to help identify errors, warnings, and performance issues in your flow design during the building process. Flow run history - Lets you go into past runs and check whether they worked, view inputs/outputs, and debug runtime problems. Find and fix errors with flow checker in Power Automate - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

options.text: Monitors flow runtime and displays execution logs in real time
options.explanation: Flow Checker does not monitor flow runtime and display execution logs in real time. Its main purpose is to analyze your flow design for errors, warnings, and performance issues before the flow is executed.

options.text: Identifies errors, warnings, and performance issues in your flow design
options.explanation: Flow Checker's primary function is to identify errors, warnings, and performance issues in your flow design. It helps you catch potential issues before running the flow, ensuring a smoother and more efficient automation process.

explanation: Flow Checker's primary function is to identify errors, warnings, and performance issues in your flow design. It helps you catch potential issues before running the flow, ensuring a smoother and more efficient automation process.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: What's the purpose of the Do Until loop?

options.text: To do the loop until a certain condition
options.explanation: The Do Until loop is designed to continue executing a set of statements until a specific condition is met. This means that the loop will keep running until the condition specified is true, allowing for repetitive tasks to be performed until a certain criteria is satisfied.

options.text: To do the loop until you stop the loop manually
options.explanation: The Do Until loop does not require manual intervention to stop the loop. It automatically stops when the specified condition becomes true, making it different from loops that require manual termination.

explanation: Exam Tips: Repeats Actions: Executes a set of actions multiple times until a specific condition is met. Condition-Based Exit: Continues looping until the condition becomes true (opposite of "While" loops). Useful for Waiting Logic: Ideal when you need to poll or wait for something to happen (e.g., a file to be created). Custom Timeout and Limits: You can configure timeouts and maximum iterations to prevent infinite loops. Supports Dynamic Conditions: Conditions can be based on variables, expressions, or outputs from previous steps.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You want to stop Dataverse from being able to connect to an email connector within Power Automate. What would you use to enforce that?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect. Security Roles in Dataverse are used to control access to data and functionality within the platform. While they are important for managing user permissions, they are not directly related to stopping a Dataverse from connecting to an email connector in Power Automate.

Data Loss Prevention Policies in Power Automate are used to prevent sensitive information from being shared or leaked outside of the organization. By configuring a Data Loss Prevention Policy, you can restrict the use of connectors, including email connectors, and prevent Dataverse from connecting to them in Power Automate.

This option is incorrect. Using a different environment in Power Automate may help in isolating and managing different sets of connectors and resources. However, simply switching to a different environment may not directly address the issue of stopping a specific Dataverse from connecting to an email connector.

explanation: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Policies in Power Platform, including Power Automate and Dataverse, are used to protect sensitive data by ensuring that it is not shared inappropriately between connectors that should not be communicating with each other. Purpose of DLP Policies: Prevent Unintended Data Sharing: DLP policies control which connectors can be used together within a flow or app. This prevents sensitive data from being sent from one service to another, like from a business-critical system to a personal or less secure service. Enforce Compliance: DLP policies ensure that data handling complies with organizational policies, industry regulations, and privacy laws. Why you need to know about DLP for PL900 exam: Security Awareness: PL-900 covers foundational knowledge, including how to build apps and automate workflows. Understanding DLP ensures you're aware of how to protect organizational data while doing so. Governance Best Practices: DLP is a key part of governance strategy. Knowing how it works helps you understand how organizations manage risk and maintain compliance when using Power Platform tools. Connector Control: DLP policies define which connectors (like SharePoint, Outlook, Twitter, etc.) can be used together. This is crucial when building apps or flows, as some combinations may be restricted. Real-World Scenarios: Many exam questions are based on practical use cases. You might be asked to identify the impact of a DLP policy or troubleshoot why a flow isn’t working due to connector restrictions. Admin vs. Maker Perspective: Even though PL-900 is a fundamentals exam, it introduces the roles of admins and makers. Makers need to understand how DLP policies affect their ability to build solutions. References: 8 Power Platform DLP Policy Best Practices

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: What can you actually administer from the Microsoft 365 admin center?

options.explanation: The Microsoft 365 Admin Center allows you to administer users within your organization. This includes creating, managing, and deleting user accounts, assigning licenses, resetting passwords, and managing user permissions and roles.

This option is incorrect. Environments are not typically administered through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center. Environments in the Power Platform are usually managed through the Power Platform Admin Center or the Power Apps Maker Portal.

This option is incorrect. Portals are not typically administered through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center. Portals in the Power Platform are usually managed through the Power Apps Maker Portal or the Dynamics 365 Admin Center.

This option is incorrect. Power Automate is not typically administered through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center. Power Automate flows and processes are usually created, managed, and monitored through the Power Automate portal or within the Power Platform environment.

explanation: Microsoft 365 Admin Center handles organizational-level management such as users, billing, and service health. Power Platform Admin Center handles Power Platform-specific services like apps, flows, and dataverse-related tasks. References: Microsoft 365 admin center - Overview - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You've shared your canvas app with Susan and made her a co-owner. Which of these is she NOT able to do?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect. As a co-owner of the Canvas App, Susan can definitely use the app as she has been granted access to it by being made a co-owner.
This option is incorrect. Being a co-owner of the Canvas App, Susan has the ability to edit the app and make changes to it as needed.
Susan, as a co-owner of the Canvas App, does not have the permission to delete the app. Only the original owner or a user with administrative privileges can delete the app.
This option is incorrect. Susan, being a co-owner of the Canvas App, can share the app with other users and grant them access to it. Sharing the app is a privilege that co-owners have.

explanation: Co-owners of a Canvas App cannot delete the app unless they are also the creator (owner) or have sufficient environment-level privileges (like Environment Admin).

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Match each policy type to its correct definition. Types: 1. Environment-level policies, 2. Tenant-level policies. Definitions: A. Applies to all environments within the organization, B. Applies only to one designated environment.
explanation: Administrators can apply DLP policies at different levels: Environment-level policies: Tailored to specific environments like development or production. Tenant-level policies: Applied across the organization for consistent protection.

text: You've edited your canvas app to add every contact's phone number to a gallery, and saved it. What happens when you go back into the canvas app?

options.text: I can now see the contacts' telephone numbers.
options.explanation: This choice suggests that after saving the changes made to the Canvas App, the contacts' telephone numbers will be visible immediately upon returning to the app.

options.text: I cannot see the contacts' telephone numbers - I need to refresh the web page.
options.explanation: This choice implies that a simple refresh of the web page is required to display the contacts' telephone numbers in the gallery after saving the changes.

options.text: I cannot see the contacts' telephone numbers no matter how many times I refresh the webpage - I need to do publish before I can see them.

Simply refreshing the webpage will not display the updated information without publishing the changes. Save and publish canvas apps - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn

explanation: Saving the App is not sufficient. You need to PUBLISH the app. Understand this information alone for PL900 exam scope. Once also need to Publish this new version or Use the Refresh() function in Power Apps to reload the data source manually. When you make changes to a data source like updating a contact’s telephone number in a form or a table and save the data using functions, the data is sent back to the data source (e.g., SharePoint, Dataverse, SQL). However, the Canvas App does not automatically refresh its display to show the updated data immediately.

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: A project manager wants application changes tested before they reach production, following a consistent deployment process. Which capability supports this?

options.explanation: Power Platform Pipelines allow project managers to create automated deployment processes that ensure application changes are tested before reaching production. They provide a consistent deployment process by allowing users to define the steps and stages for deploying applications across environments.

Security Roles are used to control access to data and functionality within the Power Platform, but they do not directly support the requirement of testing application changes before production or ensuring a consistent deployment process.

Topics in the Power Platform are used for organizing and categorizing content, such as discussions or documents, but they do not directly support the requirement of testing application changes before production or ensuring a consistent deployment process.

Business Rules in the Power Platform are used to apply logic and automation to data entry forms, but they do not directly support the requirement of testing application changes before production or ensuring a consistent deployment process.

explanation: The correct answer is A. Power Platform Pipelines. Here is why: What it is: Power Platform Pipelines are tools that automate the movement of software solutions between different environments. How it helps: They handle deploying your apps from a Development environment to a Testing (UAT) environment, and finally to Production. Real-World Analogy: Think of a pipeline like a secure airport baggage conveyor belt. It takes your luggage (your app) from the check-in desk (development) through security and screening (testing), and safely to the final destination (production) following the exact same path every single time. Key Benefit: It ensures consistency and requires that an app is successfully moved and tested in lower environments before it can ever be released to real users. Here is why the other options do not fit your specific requirement: Security Roles: These determine who can see or do things in the app, not how the app itself is moved or tested. Topics: These are used in Copilot Studio to organize conversation flows for a chatbot. Business Rules: These are simple, no-code rules used to validate data entry on a form.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A department wants a mobile-friendly app where warehouse workers can scan inventory, capture photos, and update stock levels. Which Power Apps capability fits this best?

options.explanation: A Canvas App is the best fit for this scenario as it allows for a highly customizable and flexible user interface design. It enables the creation of mobile-friendly applications with features like barcode scanning, photo capture, and data updates, making it ideal for warehouse workers to scan inventory, capture photos, and update stock levels.

A Model-driven App is not the best fit for this scenario as it is more suitable for data-driven applications with a focus on business processes and workflows. While it provides a structured way to display data and enforce business rules, it may not offer the level of customization and flexibility needed for warehouse workers to perform tasks like scanning inventory and capturing photos.

Power Pages are used for creating web pages within Power Apps portals and are not designed for mobile application development. They are more focused on external-facing content and may not provide the necessary functionality for warehouse workers to scan inventory, capture photos, and update stock levels on mobile devices.

Copilot Studio Agent is not a Power Apps capability and is not relevant to building mobile-friendly applications for warehouse workers. It is important to focus on Power Apps capabilities like Canvas Apps that are specifically designed for creating mobile applications with the required features.

explanation: The correct answer is A. Canvas App. A Canvas App allows you to build a highly customized, task-specific user interface (UI). Warehouse workers need an intuitive app that works easily on mobile phones. Canvas apps are mobile-first, can use your phone's native camera to scan barcodes, and let you capture photos to update inventory instantly. Here is why the other options do not fit best: Model-driven App: This is great for desktop-based, complex, data-centric business processes. It provides a rigid, out-of-the-box layout that does not easily support large, mobile-friendly touch buttons or camera capture controls. Power Pages: This is used to build external, public-facing websites or portals for customers or partners. It is not designed for internal warehouse scanning. Copilot Studio Agent: This is used to create conversational AI chatbots. It is not an interface meant for visual inventory management.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: What's a key feature of Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) in Power Platform?

options.explanation: The use of solutions is a key feature of Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) in Power Platform. Solutions allow developers to package and deploy components such as apps, flows, entities, and more across environments, enabling better management of changes and version control.

Weekly usage insights are not a key feature of Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) in Power Platform. While usage insights are important for monitoring and optimizing performance, they are not directly related to the management of application lifecycle.

Data policies are not a key feature of Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) in Power Platform. Data policies are more related to data governance and compliance rather than the management of application lifecycle and deployment.

Pipeline creation is not a key feature of Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) in Power Platform. While pipelines are important for automating processes and workflows, they are not specifically tied to the management of application lifecycle within the Power Platform environment.

explanation: A key feature of ALM in Power Platform is the use of solutions, which act as containers for packaging and managing application components. Solutions simplify the process of moving applications between environments (for example, development, testing, and production) and ensure that all dependencies are included. Solutions make it easier to maintain consistency, track changes, and deploy updates without disrupting the application’s functionality. References: Describe Application lifecycle Management (ALM) in Power Platform - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: What does the "Limit sharing" feature in Managed Environments let administrators do?

options.text: A) Restrict how broadly users share canvas apps
options.explanation: The "Limit sharing" feature in Managed Environments allows administrators to restrict how broadly users can share canvas apps within the environment. This helps control the dissemination of apps and ensures that sensitive information is not shared with unauthorized users.

options.text: B) Prevent users from creating new apps
options.explanation: Preventing users from creating new apps is not a functionality of the "Limit sharing" feature in Managed Environments. This feature specifically focuses on controlling the sharing of existing canvas apps within the environment.

Automatically deleting unused apps is not a capability of the "Limit sharing" feature in Managed Environments. This feature is more focused on managing the sharing permissions of apps rather than deleting them based on usage.

options.text: D) Share apps with external users only
options.explanation: The "Limit sharing" feature in Managed Environments does not specifically restrict sharing apps with external users only. It is more about controlling the sharing settings within the environment itself, regardless of whether the sharing is internal or external.

explanation: A is correct because the "Limit sharing" feature allows administrators to control how widely users can share canvas apps, such as preventing sharing with the entire organization. B is incorrect because this feature does not prevent users from creating new apps. C is incorrect because it does not automatically delete unused apps. D is incorrect because it does not focus on sharing apps with external users only. References: Describe the Power Platform admin centers and portals - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: Your company has enabled Managed Environments to improve governance, and IT wants to restrict consumer connectors like Twitter or Gmail so organizational data can't flow into them. In this context, what do Data policies in Managed Environments actually define?

text: You've built a Power Pages site and need to share Dataverse data with external users. Which TWO components in Power Pages can you use to display that data? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Forms in Power Pages allow you to display and interact with data from Dataverse in a structured manner. They provide a user-friendly way to view and edit records, making them a suitable component for displaying data to external users.

This option is incorrect. iFrames in Power Pages can be used to embed external content or web pages within the site. Therefore, they may not be the most efficient component for sharing Dataverse data with external users.

Lists in Power Pages allow you to display data from Dataverse in a tabular format, making it easy for external users to view multiple records at once. Lists provide a comprehensive view of data and are a suitable component for sharing Dataverse data with external users.

text: A company plans to roll out Copilot Studio organization-wide. Which TWO capabilities are actually part of Copilot Studio?

options.explanation: Microsoft Copilot Studio includes the capability to build conversational agents, allowing users to create chatbots and virtual assistants to interact with users.

options.text: B. Publish agents to multiple channels.
options.explanation: Microsoft Copilot Studio enables users to publish agents to multiple channels, such as websites, messaging platforms, and mobile apps, expanding the reach of the conversational agents created within the platform.

Designing Power BI reports is not a capability of Microsoft Copilot Studio. This functionality is typically associated with Power BI Desktop or Power BI Service for creating and visualizing data reports.
Creating SQL databases is not a capability of Microsoft Copilot Studio. This task is usually performed using SQL Server Management Studio or other database management tools.

Generating Excel pivot tables is not a capability of Microsoft Copilot Studio. Excel is a separate application used for data analysis and reporting, and creating pivot tables is a feature within Excel itself.

explanation: The correct answer choices are A (Build conversational agents) and B (Publish agents to multiple channels). Explanation of Correct Options A. Build conversational agents: Microsoft Copilot Studio is an end-to-end, low-code platform specifically built to allow organizations to design, customize, and create AI-powered conversational agents and custom copilots. B. Publish agents to multiple channels: Once built, the platform natively supports deploying and publishing your agents to a wide variety of channels, including Microsoft Teams, internal websites, mobile apps, Slack, or Facebook. Create SQL databases: Provisions for structured relational data are handled via databases like Azure SQL Database or Microsoft SQL Server, rather than a conversational AI building toolkit. E. Creating Topics helps Microsoft Copilot Studio agents organize and categorize information, making it easier for them to understand and respond to user queries effectively. Topics enable agents to specialize in specific areas, leading to improved quality and effectiveness in providing assistance.

Installing Power BI Desktop is not relevant to improving the quality and effectiveness of Microsoft Copilot Studio agents. Power BI Desktop is a business analytics tool used for data visualization and reporting, which does not directly impact agent performance or capabilities.

Enabling Desktop Flow Recording is not a capability that directly contributes to enhancing the quality and effectiveness of Microsoft Copilot Studio agents. Desktop Flow Recording is a feature related to automating repetitive tasks and workflows, rather than improving agent performance.

explanation: The two capabilities that directly improve the quality and effectiveness of a Microsoft Copilot Studio agent are: A. Configure Knowledge SourcesLinking your agent to specific data sources (like SharePoint, OneDrive, or websites). It allows it to "ground" its answers in your enterprise information. This ensures the agent gives accurate, relevant, and personalized responses based on your actual data rather than relying purely on generalized AI. B. Create TopicsTopics define the specific paths of a conversation between a user and the agent. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Besides building custom connectors, in what other ways can Power Automate interact with external web applications and services?

options.explanation: Power Automate Desktop is a tool used for automating repetitive tasks on a user's desktop environment. While it can interact with web applications and services through UI automation, it is not specifically designed for building Custom Connectors or integrating with external services in the same way as Power Automate.

HTTP actions in Power Automate allow users to make HTTP requests to external web services and APIs. This functionality enables Power Automate to interact with a wide range of web applications and services, making it a powerful tool for integrating different systems and automating workflows across platforms.

Web recorder is a feature in Power Automate that allows users to record their interactions with a web application and create automated workflows based on those interactions. While this can be useful for automating tasks within a specific web application, it is not as versatile as HTTP actions for interacting with a variety of external web applications and services.

explanation: Low-Code API Integration HTTP actions empower low-code developers to connect with external APIs without writing full-fledged code, bridging gaps where connectors don't exist. In Power Automate, HTTP actions allow flows to send and receive data directly to and from web services via APIs. This makes them a powerful way to interact with external systems beyond built-in connectors, perfect for scenarios where a custom connector isn’t needed or hasn’t been built yet. In simple words, Simple Example in Power Automate Suppose you want to show the current weather in Bengaluru in Teams. You add an HTTP action in your flow that calls the OpenWeather API endpoint: Code GET https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Bengaluru&appid=YOUR_API_KEY The API responds with JSON data like temperature, humidity, and conditions. Your flow parses the response and posts: “Today in Bengaluru: Sunny, 28°C.” Why others are wrong: Power Automate Desktop is used for automating tasks on a local machine, like desktop UI automation, not for web API interactions. Web recorder is a feature in Power Automate Desktop to capture UI interactions, not for calling web services.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You've built an automated flow and used your own credentials for all its connections. Now you need to hand off control of the flow to a teammate so they can enter their own credentials. What are the two most practical steps to accomplish this?

options.text: Assign your co-worker a flow admin role
options.explanation: Assigning your co-worker a flow admin role does not directly allow them to enter their credentials for the flow connections. This role typically involves managing and overseeing the flow, but it does not grant the ability to modify or enter credentials for the flow connections.

options.text: Make your co-worker co-owner of the flow
options.explanation: Making your co-worker a co-owner of the flow allows them to have control over the flow, including the ability to enter their own credentials for the flow connections. This step is practical and effective in sharing the control of the flow with your team member. Co-Owner Access Co-owners can: Edit the flow. Modify connections. Change flow logic. View run history (depending on permissions). Co-owners should be trusted users because they have significant control over the flow. Can You See a Co-Owner's Data? Not automatically. If the flow uses their connections, you do not automatically gain access to their mailbox or OneDrive. However, co-owners can modify a flow, so shared ownership should be used carefully.

options.text: Re-create a flow with your co-workers credentials
options.explanation: Re-creating a flow with your co-worker's credentials is not necessary and can be time-consuming. It is more practical to modify the existing flow connections to allow your team member to enter their credentials, rather than starting from scratch with a new flow.

options.text: Modify the flow connections to use the team member's credentials
options.explanation: Modifying flow connections is a practical step to allow your team member to enter their own credentials for the flow. This way, you can share the control of the flow with your co-worker without the need to recreate the entire flow.

explanation: The two most practical steps to allow your team member to enter their own credentials and manage the flow are: Make your co-worker co-owner of the flow = This grants them permission to edit, manage connections, and update the flow. Once they are added as a co-owner, they can provide their own credentials for the flow’s connections. Modify flow connections = After sharing ownership, your co-worker can update the connections linked to their own credentials, ensuring the flow runs under their account.
